citations.quote:
In coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$, a smooth curve $\gamma$ is a geodesic if and only if, throughout every parameter subinterval lying in the chart,
$$\ddot x^k+\Gamma^k{}_{ij}(x)\dot x^i\dot x^j=0\qquad(1\le k\le n),$$
with summation over repeated indices.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ and the chart $x=\psi_p$ on $T_0M$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Under the hypotheses of Picard-Lindelof at $(t_0,x_0)$, there are $h,r,\eta>0$ such that every initial value $(s,y)$ with $|s-t_0|<\eta$ and $\|y-x_0\|_2<\eta$ has a unique solution on $[s-h,s+h]$, and all these solution graphs lie in one compact time-state cylinder.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

Let $m\ge1$ and let $B\in\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be positive definite,
that is $B^{\mathsf T}=B$ and $z^{\mathsf T}Bz>0$ for every nonzero
$z\in\mathbb R^m$ with the standard coordinate inner product.

**(a)** There are real numbers $0<a\le b$ with $a\,|z|^2\le z^{\mathsf T}Bz\le b\,|z|^2$
for every $z\in\mathbb R^m$; equivalently $aI\le B\le bI$ in the Loewner
order. They can be taken to be the least and largest eigenvalues of $B$.

**(b)** $B$ is invertible and $\tfrac1bI\le B^{-1}\le\tfrac1aI$, so in
particular $\|B^{-1}z\|\le a^{-1}\|z\|$.

**(c)** Let $\Lambda$ be a compact topological space and let
$B:\Lambda\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ be continuous with $B(\lambda)$
positive definite for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. Then there are constants
$0<a\le b$ with $aI\le B(\lambda)\le bI$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$.

**(d)** Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ be open and let $B:D\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$
be smooth with $B(x)\ge aI$ for a constant $a>0$ and all $x\in D$. Then
$x\mapsto B(x)^{-1}$ is smooth on $D$ and $B(x)^{-1}\le a^{-1}I$ there.

Let $M$ be a smooth $n$-manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]), with smooth atlas
$\mathcal A$ and maximal smooth atlas $[\mathcal A]$
([[def-smooth-atlas]], [[def-smoothly-compatible-charts]]). For $p\in M$ the
tangent space $T_pM$ is the real vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]), and the cotangent space is its
algebraic dual $T_p^*M:=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]).

A **covariant $2$-tensor at $p$** is a bilinear map
$A_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$. It is **symmetric** when
$A_p(v,w)=A_p(w,v)$ for all $v,w\in T_pM$, and **nondegenerate** when the only
$v\in T_pM$ with $A_p(v,w)=0$ for all $w\in T_pM$ is $v=0$.

A **smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$** is a family $A=(A_p)_{p\in M}$
assigning to each $p$ a covariant $2$-tensor $A_p$ at $p$, such that for every
chart $(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas $[\mathcal A]$ the **component
functions**

$$A_{ab}(q):=A_q\!\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x^a}\Big|_q,\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x^b}\Big|_q\right),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$. Here $\partial/\partial x^a|_q$ is the coordinate
derivation at $q$ ([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]],
[[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the index
ranges over the label set $I_n=\{1,\dots,n\}$ (or the relabelled set
$I_4=\{0,1,2,3\}$ when $n=4$), and smoothness of the real-valued functions
$A_{ab}$ on the open set $U\subseteq M$ is the notion of
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] applied to $M$ and
$\mathbb R$.

For a coordinate tuple $z\in x(U)$ define the **coordinate representative**
$A^x_{ab}(z):=A_{ab}(x^{-1}(z))$. When the argument is a coordinate tuple,
$A_{ab}(z)$ abbreviates this representative in the named chart; when it is a
point of $M$, it denotes the component function on the chart domain. Thus
$A_{ab}(x(y^{-1}(u)))$ in a change-of-coordinates formula means
$A^x_{ab}((x\circ y^{-1})(u))$, never evaluation of a function on $M$ at a
tuple. For $n=4$, $x^a$ and $\partial_a$ mean the original coordinate and
derivation labelled $a+1$, respectively; this relabels every slot and sum.
The label $0$ alone gives no coordinate vector a causal character.

Because the coordinate derivations at $q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), specifying
$A$ is the same as specifying the matrix of component functions in each chart;
[[lem-gr-covariant-two-tensor-transformation-law]] proves that the smoothness
requirement is independent of the chart used, so that the condition may be
checked on any smooth atlas of $M$, and derives the transformation law relating
components in two overlapping charts.

The field is **symmetric** when $A_p$ is symmetric for every $p\in M$, which in
a chart is the identity $A_{ab}=A_{ba}$ of component functions; it is
**nondegenerate** when $A_p$ is nondegenerate for every $p$, which in a chart is
the nonvanishing at every point of the polynomial function
$\det(A_{ab})$ of the components. The **matrix** of $A$ in a chart means the
matrix $\bigl(A_{ab}(q)\bigr)$ of its component functions at $q$.

**Convention.** In the four-dimensional case $n=4$ used in this library, indices
are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ with $0$ the time-coordinate label when such a coordinate is chosen, and we write
$A_{ab}$ for the components. A covariant $2$-tensor field is also called a
**$(0,2)$ tensor field**.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T})$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]).

- An **open cover** of $(X,\mathcal{T})$ is a family
  $\mathcal{U} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ of open sets with $X = \bigcup \mathcal{U}$,
  where $\bigcup \mathcal{U} = \{\, x \in X : x \in U \text{ for some } U \in \mathcal{U} \,\}$.
- A **subcover** of $\mathcal{U}$ is a subfamily $\mathcal{V} \subseteq \mathcal{U}$
  that is itself an open cover.
- A family $\mathcal{V}$ of sets is **finite** when $\mathcal{V} = \varnothing$ or
  there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and sets $V_0, \dots, V_n$ with
  $\mathcal{V} = \{V_0, \dots, V_n\}$; repetitions in the list are allowed and
  harmless.
- $(X,\mathcal{T})$ is **compact** when every open cover of it has a finite
  subcover: for every open cover $\mathcal{U}$, either $X = \varnothing$ and the
  empty subfamily covers it, or there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and
  $U_0, \dots, U_n \in \mathcal{U}$ with
  $$X = U_0 \cup \dots \cup U_n .$$
- A subset $A \subseteq X$ is a **compact subset** of $X$ when the subspace
  $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ is a compact topological space, $\mathcal{T}_A$ being the
  subspace topology ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).

**Compactness of a subset is defined intrinsically, and only intrinsically.**
The last clause speaks about the subspace $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ and its own open
sets, not about families of open subsets of the ambient $X$. The two readings do
agree, but that is a theorem and not a convention: it is
[[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]], and no item of this library may use
the ambient reading without citing it. Taking the intrinsic reading makes
compactness a property of the topological space $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ alone.
Hence it is preserved when $A$ is embedded homeomorphically as a subspace, or
when another ambient space induces the same topology on $A$; it need not be
preserved if the induced topology changes. This is exactly the convention already fixed for
metric spaces by [[def-metric-compactness]], and the agreement of that
definition with this one is [[thm-compactness-agrees-with-metric-compactness]].

**The empty space is compact**, since the empty subfamily of any family covers
it; this is the reason the clause above is written with the two cases. Every
space listed as $\{x_0, \dots, x_n\}$ is compact too: given a cover, each $x_i$
lies in some member, and finitely many members named in this way already cover.
So every finite space is compact, whatever its topology, and in particular the
discrete topology on a finite set is compact while the discrete topology on an
infinite set is not ([[def-standard-topologies]]).

**The finiteness convention.** "Finite" above is the listing form. It agrees with
the definition of finiteness by equinumerosity with a natural number
([[def-countable]]), in both directions, and the agreement is the one already
discharged in [[def-metric-compactness]]: a nonempty set equinumerous with
$m \ge 1$ is listable, and a set listed as $\{a_0, \dots, a_n\}$ injects into
$\sigma(n)$ by sending $x$ to the least $i \le n$ with $a_i = x$. Neither
direction uses a choice principle; the second selects nothing, taking a least
index instead.

**Quasicompact is not used here.** Some authors, following Bourbaki, reserve
*compact* for a space that is both compact in the above sense and Hausdorff, and
call the open-cover condition alone *quasicompact*. This library follows the more
widely adopted convention: **compact** means the open-cover condition and nothing
more, and a Hausdorff hypothesis is always written out. The fork is recorded in
[[rem-compactness-conventions-and-choice-ledger]].

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field with its order and
absolute value ([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[lem-of-abs-value]]), and
neighbourhoods are those of [[def-neighbourhood-r]].

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $c \in A$. Then
$f$ is **continuous at $c$** when

$$(\forall \varepsilon > 0)\ (\exists \delta > 0)\ (\forall x \in A)\ \bigl[\ |x - c| < \delta \ \Longrightarrow\ |f(x) - f(c)| < \varepsilon\ \bigr],$$

with $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$ ranging over the **positive reals**. In the
language of neighbourhoods: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real
$\delta > 0$ with

$$f\bigl(A \cap N_{\delta}(c)\bigr) \;\subseteq\; N_{\varepsilon}\bigl(f(c)\bigr).$$

$f$ is **continuous on $A$** when it is continuous at every point of $A$.

**The point $c$ is required to lie in $A$, and the condition is unpunctured.**
Both differ from [[def-function-limit]], and deliberately. There the quantifier
runs over $0 < |x - c| < \delta$, which removes $x = c$; here $x = c$ is allowed,
and at $x = c$ the implication reads $|f(c) - f(c)| = 0 < \varepsilon$, which is
automatic. So allowing $x = c$ costs nothing, and it is what lets the definition
be stated at every point of $A$, including the points where no limit exists.

**Three clauses, and all three are part of the definition.**

1. **At a limit point.** Suppose $c \in A$ is a limit point of $A$
   ([[def-limit-point-r]]). Then $f$ is continuous at $c$ if and only if the
   limit of $f$ at $c$ exists and
   $$\lim_{x \to c} f(x) \;=\; f(c)$$
   ([[def-function-limit]]). Indeed, for a given $\varepsilon > 0$ a $\delta$
   witnessing continuity witnesses the limit condition, because the limit
   condition quantifies over a subset of the points continuity quantifies over;
   and conversely a $\delta$ witnessing $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)$ witnesses
   continuity, because the one point it omits, $x = c$, satisfies
   $|f(c) - f(c)| < \varepsilon$ anyway.

2. **At an isolated point.** Suppose $c \in A$ is an isolated point of $A$
   ([[def-limit-point-r]]), so that $N_{\eta}(c) \cap A = \{c\}$ for some real
   $\eta > 0$. Then **every** $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous at $c$: take
   $\delta := \eta$, so that the only $x \in A$ with $|x - c| < \delta$ is $c$
   itself, and $|f(c) - f(c)| = 0 < \varepsilon$.

3. **On a set.** Continuity on $A$ is continuity at each point of $A$, and
   nothing more. It is not a condition relating $f$ to points outside $A$.

Every point of $A$ is either a limit point of $A$ or an isolated point of $A$,
and never both ([[def-limit-point-r]]), so clauses 1 and 2 between them describe
continuity at every point of $A$.

**This is not the raw $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ formula of
[[fs-limit-unique-at-every-point-of-the-domain]].** That item records what goes
wrong when the *punctured* formula of [[def-function-limit]] is written down at
an arbitrary point of the domain: at an isolated point it is satisfied
vacuously by every real $L$ at once, so it defines nothing, and this library
therefore leaves $\lim_{x \to c} f(x)$ **undefined** at an isolated point.
Continuity at an isolated point is a different matter: the formula above is not
vacuous — it is a genuine condition on $f(c)$, satisfied because $f(c)$ is the
only value being compared with itself — and it names a single, well-defined
property. The limit is undefined there; the continuity is defined, and is
automatic. Clause 1 is the only place where the two notions meet, and it is
stated only where the limit exists as a notion.

**Where the distinction disappears.** If $A$ is an open subset of $\mathbb{R}$
([[def-open-and-closed-in-r]]), then every $c \in A$ has some
$N_{\eta}(c) \subseteq A$, and a punctured neighbourhood is never empty
([[def-neighbourhood-r]]), so every point of $A$ is a limit point of $A$ and
clause 1 covers the whole of $A$. The same holds when $A$ is a nondegenerate
interval ([[def-interval]]). Isolated points are what force clause 2 to exist at
all, and they occur as soon as $A$ is allowed to be an arbitrary subset of
$\mathbb{R}$, as in $A = \{0\} \cup [1,2]$.

(The rescaled velocity.) A nonconstant geodesic has no zero velocity at any parameter: a zero-velocity datum launches the constant solution, and ODE uniqueness would make the entire maximal solution constant. Therefore its $h$-speed is positive.  Let $\gamma:J	o M$ be a nonconstant geodesic with affine parameter $\lambda$ and let $\ell$ be $h$-arclength, so $d\ell/d\lambda=q>0$. Write $v:=d\gamma/d\ell$ for the $h$-unit velocity of $\gamma$ and $u:=d\gamma/d\lambda=q\,v$ for the affine velocity. Since $\gamma$ is a geodesic, $
abla_uu=0$, hence $
abla_vv=\sigma v$ for the function $\sigma:=-d\log q/d\ell$: indeed $
abla_{qv}(qv)=q^2
abla_vv+q\,v(q)\,v$, so $
abla_vv=- rac{v(q)}{q}v$ and $v(q)=dq/d\ell$ because $q$ is a function of $\ell$ along the curve.

(Derivative of the $h$-speed.) Covariant differentiation along the reparametrized curve gives $
abla_vu=q^{-1}
abla_uu=0$; equivalently $
abla_v(qv)=q'v+q
abla_vv=0$ by step 1.1. Thus the tensor product rule gives $ rac{d}{d\ell}h(u,u)=(
abla_vh)(u,u)+2h(
abla_vu,u)=(
abla_vh)(u,u)$. Since $h(u,u)=q^2$, one obtains $2q\,q'=(
abla_vh)(u,u)$.

(The bound.) Let $K$ be compact. By [L2] there is $\kappa(K)<\infty$ with $|(\nabla_Z h)(X,Y)|\le\kappa(K)|X|_h|Y|_h|Z|_h$ for all points of $K$ and all tangent vectors there. On the parameters with $\gamma(\ell)\in K$: $|(\nabla_v h)(u,u)|\le\kappa(K)|u|_h^2|v|_h=\kappa(K)q^2$, so by step 2.1, $2q|q'|\le\kappa(K)q^2$, that is, $|d\log q/d\ell|\le\kappa(K)/2$ there. This proves (a) with $c(K):=\kappa(K)/2$.

(Bounds on the affine data up to the endpoint.) In the situation of clause (b), let $L:=\int_{\lambda_0}^{\beta}|\gamma'|_h\,d\lambda<\infty$ be the finite tail length and put $\ell(\lambda):=\int_{\lambda_0}^{\lambda}|\gamma'|_h\,dt$, a strictly increasing smooth map $[\lambda_0,\beta)\to[0,L)$ with smooth inverse, so $\ell\to L$ as $\lambda\to\beta$. By clause (a) applied on the tail, with $\gamma([\lambda_0,\beta))\subseteq K$, one has $q(\ell)\le q(0)e^{c(K)L}=:M$ and $q(\ell)\ge q(0)e^{-c(K)L}=:m>0$ for all $\ell\in[0,L)$.

(A compact set of bounded affine data.) The set $B:=\{(x,w)\in TM:x\in K,\ |w|_h\le M\}$ is compact. Indeed take finitely many compact chart pieces covering $K$, each contained in a tangent-bundle trivialization; such pieces are obtained by shrinking coordinate balls and taking a finite subcover of $K$. On each piece [L2] bounds the Euclidean velocity coordinates by $M/\sqrt{m_j}$, and the condition $h_x(w,w)\le M^2$ cuts out a closed subset of the product of that compact piece and a closed Euclidean ball. Each resulting set is compact, and their finite union is $B$. Step 4.1 puts every affine datum $(\gamma(\lambda),\gamma'(\lambda))$ on the tail in $B$. No sequence or subsequence of velocities is selected.

(Uniform ODE continuation.) Apply [L1] to the smooth first-order geodesic vector field in tangent-bundle charts. At every datum in $B$ it supplies a neighborhood of initial data and a positive common existence time in that chart. Take a finite subcover of $B$ by all such neighborhoods and let $\delta>0$ be smaller than their finitely many times. Every datum in $B$ therefore launches a geodesic for at least time $\delta$. Fix $\lambda_*\in(\lambda_0,\beta)$ with $\beta-\lambda_*<\delta/2$. The solution launched from $(\gamma(\lambda_*),\gamma'(\lambda_*))$ exists past $\beta$ and agrees with $\gamma$ on their overlap by uniqueness. Gluing it to the earlier part extends the affine geodesic beyond $\beta$, contradicting maximality and proving (b). This uses only a finite subcover and finite minima, so no choice principle is needed.

Statement: Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let geodesics
be the maximal geodesics with their affine parametrizations supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Let $h$ be a smooth
positive definite metric on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

**(a)** For every compact $K\subseteq M$ there is a constant $c(K)\in[0,\infty)$
with the following property. Let $\gamma:J\to M$ be a nonconstant geodesic,
let $q>0$ be the $h$-speed of its affine velocity and let $\ell$ denote the
$h$-arclength parameter of $\gamma$, so that $q(\ell):=|d\gamma/d\lambda|_h$
is the $h$-norm of the affine velocity expressed in the parameter $\ell$. At
every parameter value with $\gamma(\ell)\in K$ one has
$$\left|\frac{d\log q}{d\ell}\right|\le c(K).$$

**(b)** Assume in addition that $(M,d_h)$ is complete and that every closed
$d_h$-bounded subset of $M$ is compact. Let $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ be a
maximal nonconstant geodesic with $\beta<+\infty$, let $\lambda_0\in(\alpha,\beta)$,
and let $K\subseteq M$ be compact with $\gamma([\lambda_0,\beta))\subseteq K$.
Suppose that the $h$-arclength of the tail is finite:
$$\int_{\lambda_0}^{\beta}\bigl|\gamma'(\lambda)\bigr|_h\,d\lambda<\infty .$$
Then the geodesic extends beyond $\beta$, contradicting the maximality of
$(\alpha,\beta)$; consequently no maximal geodesic can have a finite affine
endpoint while its tail remains in a compact set and has finite
$h$-arclength. This is a conditional assertion; it promises no converse characterization of its hypotheses. The iff-forward case has no additional implication to prove.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and suppose there exists a Cauchy set
$S\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause
(c)): every inextendible causal curve meets $S$ in exactly one parameter
value. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve with equal endpoints
(so $(M,g,N)$ is causal and chronological in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a));

**(b)** $(M,g,N)$ is strongly causal (clause (b) of that definition);

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold that is globally hyperbolic in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(c): strongly causal and with compact causal diamonds
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ for all $p,q\in M$. Let $h$ be the auxiliary metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] and let $\le$, $J^\pm$ be the
relations of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** the causal relation is closed: if $p_k\le q_k$ for all $k$ and
$p_k\to p$, $q_k\to q$, then $p\le q$; consequently $J^+(x)$ and $J^-(x)$
are closed for every $x$, and so are $J^+(K)$ and $J^-(K)$ for every compact
$K\subseteq M$;

**(b)** for all compact $K_1,K_2\subseteq M$ the set
$J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ is compact.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$
with $\delta(a)=\delta(b)$; in particular $S$ is achronal and acausal, and
the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of
$S$ chronologically precedes $x$;

**(b)** $S$ is closed in $M$;

**(c)** for every $p\in S$ there are a chart $(U,x)$ of the kind produced by
[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with
$x(p)=0$ and the supplier constants $K\ge1$ and $c=16$, and numbers $a,\rho,\eta>0$ with $\sqrt c\,\rho+\eta<a$ and
$W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$ such that for every
$z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$L_z=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$ meets $S\cap W$ in exactly one
point $x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$, and
$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $|\varphi(z)|\le\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. The cylinder $W$ may be chosen inside any prescribed neighborhood of $p$. Consequently the maps
$z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ form a topological atlas on the closed set
$S$, making $S$ a topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology whose
inclusion into $M$ is a topological embedding.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$, $I^\pm=I^\pm_M$ and
$I'^\pm=I^\pm_{M'}$. Then:

**(a)** $\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is achronal in $M$, and
$\partial\varphi(U)\cap I'^+(\Sigma')$ is achronal in $M'$.

**(b)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding
boundary points to the future of the initial surface. Then
$$\varphi\bigl(I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U),$$
and for every $q\in I^-(p)\cap U$ also
$$\varphi\bigl(I^+(q)\cap I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^+(\varphi(q))\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U).$$

**(c)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding.
If $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,0)\to U$ is a future timelike curve with
$\gamma(s)\to p$ as $s\nearrow0$, then $\varphi(\gamma(s))\to p'$ as
$s\nearrow0$. Moreover $p$ has at most one corresponding boundary point.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) for the supplied causal-calculus and Cauchy-side
results used below.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ be as in
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a): $M$ is
a development of the given data, $U\subseteq M$ is open with
$j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$, and $U$ with the restricted fields is again a
development of the same data. Write $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and compute
$I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ and $\le$ in $M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Then:

**(a) Past convexity within the future of $\Sigma$.** For every future causal
curve $\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a)\in\Sigma$ and $\nu(b)\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$
one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

**(b) Future convexity within the past of $\Sigma$.** For every future causal
curve $\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a)\in U\cap I^-(\Sigma)$ and
$\nu(b)\in\Sigma$ one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

**(c) Segments with endpoints in $U$.** For every future causal curve
$\nu:[a,b]\to M$ with $\nu(a),\nu(b)\in U$ one has $\nu([a,b])\subseteq U$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $C\subseteq M$ be a strictly
convex normal set ([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]]
clause (b)), let $p\in C$, and write
$$W_p:=\exp_p^{-1}(C)\subseteq T_pM,\qquad v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q),\qquad P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q)),\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q)).$$
Define
$$J_C^+(p):=\{p\}\cup\{q\in C:\text{there is a future causal curve } \sigma:[0,1]\to C\text{ with }\sigma(0)=p,\ \sigma(1)=q\},$$
so the reflexive endpoint $p$ is included even though a constant curve is
not in the curve class. Define
$$I_C^+(p):=\{q\in C:\text{there is a future timelike curve } \sigma:[0,1]\to C\text{ with }\sigma(0)=p,\ \sigma(1)=q\}$$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Put
$$\mathcal C^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future causal or }v=0\},\quad \mathcal T^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future timelike}\},\quad \mathcal N^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future null and }v\ne0\}.$$
Then:

**(a) Causal containment.** For every future causal curve
$\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ with $\sigma(0)=p$, the position vector
$v(\sigma(t))$ is future causal or zero for every $t\in[0,1]$.

**(b) Cone characterizations.**
$$J^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal C^+),\qquad I^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal T^+),\qquad J^+_C(p)\setminus\bigl(I^+_C(p)\cup\{p\}\bigr)=\exp_p(\mathcal N^+).$$

**(c) Null rigidity.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$, and let $\hat s\in(0,1]$ satisfy: $v(\sigma(\hat s))$ is
future null nonzero and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for every $t\in(0,\hat s]$. Then
there are $v_0\in\mathcal N^+$ and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous
surjection $\varphi:[0,\hat s]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for $0\le t\le\hat s$.

**(d) Length maximality.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$. Then
$$L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-D_p^2\bigl(\sigma(1)\bigr)}=\sqrt{-g_p\bigl(v(\sigma(1)),v(\sigma(1))\bigr)} .$$
If moreover $v(\sigma(1))$ is future timelike and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for all
$t\in(0,1]$, then equality holds if and only if there are $v_0$ future
timelike and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous surjection
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for all $t$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$ and let $C$ be a strictly convex normal ball around $p$ satisfying
the hypotheses of [[thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone]], with the
exponential chart $u$, the position vector $P(p,q)$ and
$D_p^2(q)=g_p(\exp_p^{-1}q,\exp_p^{-1}q)$. Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be a
future causal curve with $\sigma(0)=p$ and suppose that
$D_p^2(\sigma(t_0))=0$ for some $t_0\in(0,1]$. Then:

**(a)** $D_p^2(\sigma(t))=0$ for every $t\in[0,t_0]$, and
$u^0(\sigma(t))\ge0$;

**(b)** the velocity $\sigma'(t)$ is null (or does not exist) for almost
every $t\in[0,t_0]$, and consequently $L_g(\sigma|_{[0,t_0]})=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ and the relations $\ll$, $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** if $p\ll q$ and $q\le r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(b)** if $p\le q$ and $q\ll r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(c)** if $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is a future causal curve and there are
$a\le s<t\le b$ such that $\gamma|_{[s,t]}$ is a future timelike curve, then
$\gamma(a)\ll\gamma(b)$;

**(d)** consequently
$$I^+\bigl(J^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega),\qquad I^-\bigl(J^-(\Omega)\bigr)=I^-(\Omega)$$
for every $\Omega\subseteq M$, and dually
$J^+\bigl(I^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega)$.

No choice principle is used.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, with the
relations $\ll$, $\le$ and the sets $I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] and the future and past sets of
[[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]]. Then:

**(a) Openness.** For every $x\in M$ the chronological future $I^+(x)$ and
the chronological past $I^-(x)$ are open subsets of $M$.

**(b) The chronological relation is open.** The set
$$\{(x,y)\in M\times M:\ x\ll y\}$$
is open in the product topology of $M\times M$.

**(c) Closure of future and past sets.** Let $F\subseteq M$ be a future set,
that is $I^+(F)\subseteq F$. Then every $q\in\overline F$ satisfies
$I^+(q)\subseteq F$. Dually, if $P$ is a past set ($I^-(P)\subseteq P$) and
$q\in\overline P$, then $I^-(q)\subseteq P$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.

3. **Geodesic speed and proper time.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the function
   $t\mapsto g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))$ is constant. If $\gamma$
   is nonconstant, its tangent is nowhere zero and its causal character
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant; a constant geodesic has zero
   tangent and is assigned none of those causal characters. If $\gamma$ is a
   **future-directed timelike geodesic** and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then for
   $t_0<t_1$ its proper-time increment over $[t_0,t_1]$ is
   $\lambda(t_1-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter. In this parameter its four-velocity is
   $U=(c/\lambda)\gamma'$ and is parallel: $D_\tau U=0$. Proper time is not
   assigned to a past-directed curve by that definition; reversing the
   parameter gives a future-directed timelike geodesic with the same
   (positive) proper-time magnitude. A nonconstant null geodesic has null
   tangent and admits no proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic whose
   tangent is nowhere zero, and let $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto
   its open image with $h'\neq0$. Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and
   only if $h(s)=as+b$ with constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the
   constant $h'$, and every affine parameter of this nonconstant geodesic
   arises in this way from a fixed one. If $\gamma$ is constant, then
   $\gamma\circ h$ is constant and hence geodesic for every such $h$; no
   affine restriction on $h$ follows.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$$C:=\{p\in\partial U:\ p\text{ has a corresponding boundary point in }\partial\varphi(U)\}$$
be the set of boundary points of $U$ that have a corresponding point (clause
(c) of that definition). Then:

**(a)** $C$ is open in $\partial U$: there is an open set $G\subseteq M$ with
$C=G\cap\partial U$.

**(b)** There is an open set $\Omega\subseteq M$ with $U\cup C\subseteq\Omega$
and a smooth map $\Phi:\Omega\to M'$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\varphi$ and
whose value at $p\in C$ is the unique corresponding boundary point of $p$;
moreover, for every $p\in C$ there is an open neighbourhood
$W_p\subseteq\Omega$ of $p$ and a smooth **local diffeomorphism**
$$\widehat\varphi_p:W_p\to M',\qquad \widehat\varphi_p(q)=\exp_{\varphi(a_p)}\bigl(d\varphi_{a_p}(\exp_{a_p}^{-1}q)\bigr)$$
built from a common interior base point $a_p\in U$, chosen in $I^-(p)$ when $p$ is to the future of the initial surface and in $I^+(p)$ when $p$ is to its past, and the
exponential maps, such that $\widehat\varphi_p=\varphi$ on $W_p\cap U$ and
$\Phi=\widehat\varphi_p$ on $W_p\cap(U\cup C)$. No isometry property of
$\widehat\varphi_p$ on the part of $W_p$ outside $\overline U$ is claimed.

**(c)** At every point $q\in U\cup C$ the map $\Phi$ preserves the metric, the
matter fields and the metric-selected connection:

1. $g'_{\Phi(q)}(d\Phi_qv,d\Phi_qw)=g_q(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_qM$, so
   $\Phi^*(g')=g$ on $U\cup C$;
2. $(\Phi^*\psi'^i)_q=\psi^i_q$ for every listed matter field $i$;
3. for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ defined on a neighbourhood of $q$ and
   every $q\in U\cup C$,
   $$\nabla'_{d\Phi\,X}d\Phi\,Y=d\Phi\bigl(\nabla_XY\bigr)\quad\text{at }\Phi(q),$$
   equivalently the pullback connection $\Phi^*\nabla'$ equals $\nabla$ at
   $q$, where both sides are read through the invertible differential
   $d\Phi_q$.

**(d)** Every geodesic segment of $(M,g)$ whose image is contained in $U\cup C$
is mapped by $\Phi$ to a geodesic segment of $(M',g')$; a null geodesic
segment is mapped to a null geodesic segment.

**(e)** Let $S\subseteq U\cup C$ be an embedded submanifold of $M$. Then
$\Phi|_S$ is an injective immersion, hence an embedding onto its image, and it
carries the induced metric of $S$, its second fundamental form with respect to
any unit normal field, and the matter fields together with their covariant derivatives of every finite order along $S$ to the corresponding objects of $\Phi(S)$ in
$M'$. In particular $(S,\bar g_S,k_S,\psi|_S)$ and
$(\Phi(S),\bar g_{\Phi(S)},k_{\Phi(S)},\psi'|_{\Phi(S)})$ are identified by
$\Phi|_S$ whenever $S$ is spacelike.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$, $I^\pm=I^\pm_M$ and
$I'^\pm=I^\pm_{M'}$. Then:

**(a)** $\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is achronal in $M$, and
$\partial\varphi(U)\cap I'^+(\Sigma')$ is achronal in $M'$.

**(b)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding
boundary points to the future of the initial surface. Then
$$\varphi\bigl(I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U),$$
and for every $q\in I^-(p)\cap U$ also
$$\varphi\bigl(I^+(q)\cap I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^+(\varphi(q))\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U).$$

**(c)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding.
If $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,0)\to U$ is a future timelike curve with
$\gamma(s)\to p$ as $s\nearrow0$, then $\varphi(\gamma(s))\to p'$ as
$s\nearrow0$. Moreover $p$ has at most one corresponding boundary point.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ be a development of the given data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a), write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $h$ be the auxiliary complete metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]. Then for every $q\in M$ the
set
$$K_q:=J^-(q)\cap J^+(\Sigma)$$
is compact. Moreover $K_q=\{q\}$ when $q\in\Sigma$, and $K_q$ is empty when
$q\in I^-(\Sigma)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}}\quad\text{(pointwise)},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat,$$
with the flat map $\flat$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
so that $h$ is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then:

**(a)** $h$ is a smooth Riemannian (positive definite) metric on $M$.

**(b)** There is a smooth nonnegative proper function $f:M\to[0,\infty)$ such
that the metric
$$h':=(1+|df|_h^2)\,h$$
is a smooth Riemannian metric with $|df|_{h'}\le1$ everywhere.

**(c)** For each connected component $M_0$ of $M$, the metric space
$(M_0,d_{h'})$ is complete, where $d_{h'}$ is the Riemannian distance of
$h'|_{M_0}$ ([[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]],
[[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]]).

**(d)** Consequently, for every connected component $M_0$, every subset of
$M_0$ that is closed in $M_0$ and bounded in $d_{h'}$ is compact, and every
closed ball $\{q\in M_0:d_{h'}(q,p)\le r\}$ is compact.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous curve calculus and its fundamental theorem. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a strongly causal time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(b)) and let $h$ be a smooth positive definite metric on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then for every compact set
$K\subseteq M$ there is $L(K)\in[0,\infty)$ such that
$$\ell_h(\gamma)\le L(K)$$
for every future causal curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) with $\gamma([a,b])\subseteq K$.

Consequently, if $\gamma$ is parametrized by $h$-arclength
($\ell_h(\gamma|_{[s,t]})=t-s$) and its image is contained in the compact set
$K$, then $b-a\le L(K)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let geodesics
be the maximal geodesics with their affine parametrizations supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Let $h$ be a smooth
positive definite metric on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]).

**(a)** For every compact $K\subseteq M$ there is a constant $c(K)\in[0,\infty)$
with the following property. Let $\gamma:J\to M$ be a nonconstant geodesic,
let $q>0$ be the $h$-speed of its affine velocity and let $\ell$ denote the
$h$-arclength parameter of $\gamma$, so that $q(\ell):=|d\gamma/d\lambda|_h$
is the $h$-norm of the affine velocity expressed in the parameter $\ell$. At
every parameter value with $\gamma(\ell)\in K$ one has
$$\left|\frac{d\log q}{d\ell}\right|\le c(K).$$

**(b)** Assume in addition that $(M,d_h)$ is complete and that every closed
$d_h$-bounded subset of $M$ is compact. Let $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ be a
maximal nonconstant geodesic with $\beta<+\infty$, let $\lambda_0\in(\alpha,\beta)$,
and let $K\subseteq M$ be compact with $\gamma([\lambda_0,\beta))\subseteq K$.
Suppose that the $h$-arclength of the tail is finite:
$$\int_{\lambda_0}^{\beta}\bigl|\gamma'(\lambda)\bigr|_h\,d\lambda<\infty .$$
Then the geodesic extends beyond $\beta$, contradicting the maximality of
$(\alpha,\beta)$; consequently no maximal geodesic can have a finite affine
endpoint while its tail remains in a compact set and has finite
$h$-arclength.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be two developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]].

**(a) Common subdevelopment.** A **common subdevelopment** of $M$ and $M'$ is
a pair $(U,\varphi)$ in which

1. $U\subseteq M$ is an open subset with $j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$ such that the
   restriction $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ is a development of the same data
   (with the induced field equations on the open submanifold $U$); and
2. $\varphi:(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)\to(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a development
   embedding in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
   clause (c).

Here "the induced field equations on $U$" means the equations of clause (a)4
of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] restricted to $U$; the
induced Lorentzian manifold is $(U,g|_U)$ with the time orientation $N|_U$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(b) Maximal common development.** A common subdevelopment $(U^*,\varphi^*)$
is a **maximal common development** (MCD) of $M$ and $M'$ when for every
common subdevelopment $(U,\varphi)$ one has $U\subseteq U^*$ and
$\varphi^*|_U=\varphi$. Existence is not asserted by this definition; it is
proved in [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]].

**(c) Corresponding boundary points.** Let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common
subdevelopment. Its **corresponding boundary points** are pairs
$(p,p')\in\partial^M U\times\partial^{M'}\varphi(U)$, where the boundaries are
taken in $M$ and in $M'$ respectively, such that for every open neighbourhood
$V$ of $p$ in $M$ and every open neighbourhood $V'$ of $p'$ in $M'$ there is
$x\in V\cap U$ with $\varphi(x)\in V'$.

**(d) Side of the initial surface.** Write $\Sigma_M=j(\Sigma)$ and
$\Sigma_{M'}=j'(\Sigma)$. For a corresponding pair $(p,p')$, openness of
$U\supseteq\Sigma_M$ and of $\varphi(U)\supseteq\Sigma_{M'}$ implies
$p\notin\Sigma_M$ and $p'\notin\Sigma_{M'}$.
The Cauchy-set trichotomy and chronology openness of
[[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]] clauses (a),(b) therefore put each
boundary point in exactly one of the open chronological sides.
For $x\in U$, its ambient and intrinsic sides agree: the trichotomy in
$U$ gives an intrinsic timelike curve between $x$ and $\Sigma_M$ in one
direction, and that curve is also an ambient curve; the disjoint ambient
trichotomy excludes the other direction. The development embedding
$\varphi$ preserves these curves and the initial surface, so corresponding
interior points have matching ambient sides in $M$ and $M'$.
Choose neighbourhoods of $p,p'$ contained in their respective sides.
Condition (c) supplies an interior witness $x$ in both neighbourhoods under
$\varphi$; hence the two sides must match. Every witness for neighbourhoods
contained in these sides then has this same sign. Thus the pair lies either
to the **future** of both initial surfaces or to their **past**, with no
cofinal witnesses of the opposite sign. The future case is used below;
the past case is its time reverse.

**(e) Scope.** These are mathematical relations between two fixed developments
and their boundary points. Neither the existence of boundary points, nor the
existence of a common subdevelopment with nonempty boundary, nor uniqueness of
a corresponding point, is asserted here.

derivations.claim: (An initial boundary generator.) Choose $p_0\in C\cap J^+(\Sigma)$. Because $\Sigma\subseteq U$, the splitting in [L1] gives $p_0\in I^+(\Sigma)$. If the displayed exposed-point property already holds, take $p=p_0$. Otherwise choose a distinct $q_0\in J^-(p_0)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ and a causal curve joining them. Achronality [L2] and the null-versus-timelike alternative [L3] make this a null geodesic segment. Parametrize its maximal extension $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ in the past direction with $\gamma(0)=p_0$ and $\gamma(1)=q_0$. By [L4] it meets $\Sigma$ once, at a parameter $T>1$: a crossing at $T\le1$ would imply $q_0\in J^-(\Sigma)\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\Sigma$, impossible. All points $\gamma(t)$ for $0\le t<T$ lie in $I^+(\Sigma)$, because they are causally after $\gamma(T)\in\Sigma$, are not on $\Sigma$, and [L1] excludes the past side.

(No interior complement point below a future boundary.) Let $x\in\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and suppose $r\in\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with $r\le x$. Since $\Sigma\subseteq U$, one has $r\in I^+(\Sigma)$. Choose a sufficiently small past timelike perturbation $r_-\ll r$ inside the open set $\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. Push-up gives $r_-\ll x$. The open neighborhood $I^+(r_-)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ of $x$ meets $U$, at $s$ say. Concatenate a timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $r_-$ with one from $r_-$ to $s$. Past convexity [L2] puts this entire curve in $U$, contradicting $r_-\notin U$. Thus no such $r$ exists. The perturbation is to the past, so the push-up direction is valid.

(Boundary-to-boundary causal segments stay on the boundary.) Let $y\le x$ be future boundary points and let $\eta$ be a future causal segment from $y$ to $x$. Every point $z$ of the segment lies in $I^+(\Sigma)$: some $\sigma\in\Sigma$ has $\sigma\ll y\le z$. If $z\in U$, concatenate a timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $y$ with the segment from $y$ to $z$; past convexity [L2] would give $y\in U$. If $z\in\operatorname{int}(U^c)$, step 1.2 with $z\le x$ gives a contradiction. Thus every point lies in $\partial U$. Achronality and [L3] further make every nonconstant such segment a null geodesic.

(The actual last boundary parameter before the Cauchy crossing.) Set $B:=\{t\in[0,T]:\gamma(t)\in\partial U\}$. It is closed in the compact interval $[0,T]$, contains $[0,1]$ by step 2.1, and misses a neighborhood of $T$ because $\gamma(T)\in\Sigma\subseteq U$. Whenever $t\in B$, step 2.1 applied to $\gamma(t)\le\gamma(0)$ puts $[0,t]$ in $B$. Therefore $B=[0,b]$ for its maximum $b$, with $1\le b<T<\beta$. In particular the whole segment $\gamma([0,b])$ is future boundary, and no parameter in $(b,T]$ is a boundary parameter. This establishes the interval property instead of assuming it for a closed preimage.

(Follow only the initial connected component of corresponding points.) Let $J:=\{t\in[0,b]:\gamma(t)\in C\}$. It is relatively open and contains $0$ by [L5]. Define $s:=\sup\{t\in[0,b]:[0,t]\subseteq J\}$; relative openness at $0$ gives $s>0$, and every $0\le t<s$ belongs to $J$. On the interval $[0,s)$, the curve $f\circ\gamma=\Phi\circ\gamma$ is a past null affine geodesic by [L5]. Let $\eta$ be its unique maximal geodesic extension in $M'$, with the same parameter and initial data at $0$. Local uniqueness and connectedness give $\eta(t)=f(\gamma(t))$ for all $0\le t<s$; equivalently the interval solution itself is a restriction of the maximal solution. Each such value is a corresponding future boundary point, and hence belongs to $K':=J'^-(f(p_0))\cap J'^+(\Sigma')$, which is compact by [L6]. No connectedness of the entire open set $J$ has been assumed.

(Continuation of the image at the first possible exit.) The right endpoint $\beta'$ of the maximal domain of $\eta$ satisfies $\beta'\ge s$. If $\beta'=s$, its tail $\eta([0,s))$ lies in $K'$. On the component containing that curve choose the auxiliary complete proper metric $h'$ from [L6]; $K'$ intersected with this component is compact, since connected components of a manifold are closed. Strong causality gives a uniform length bound for every subsegment $\eta([0,t])$, $t<s$. Taking the supremum of these integrals gives finite $h'$-length of the entire tail. Since $s\le b<\infty$, the compact-length affine extension theorem [L6] extends $\eta$ beyond $s$, a contradiction. Thus $\beta'>s$, and $\eta(s)$ is an actual smooth geodesic value with $\eta(t)\to\eta(s)$ as $t\uparrow s$.

(The first exit is still corresponding.) As $t\uparrow s$, the corresponding pairs $(\gamma(t),\eta(t))$ converge to $(\gamma(s),\eta(s))$. Their source values lie in $\partial U$ and their target values in $\partial\varphi(U)$; both boundaries are closed. Step 3.1 already gives $\gamma(s)\in\partial U$, and closedness gives $\eta(s)\in\partial\varphi(U)$. For any neighborhoods of these two limits, sufficiently late values of the pair lie in both neighborhoods; [L7] then supplies an interior witness for the same neighborhoods. Hence the limit pair is corresponding, and $s\in J$. If $s<b$, relative openness gives an interval to the right of $s$ in $J$, which together with $[0,s]\subseteq J$ contradicts the definition of $s$. Therefore $s=b$, and $p:=\gamma(b)$ belongs to $C\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. In particular all of $[0,b]$ lies in $J$. The map used at boundary points throughout is $f$ or $\Phi$, never the interior map $\varphi$ evaluated off its domain.

(Expose the final boundary point.) Suppose a distinct $q\in J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ existed. By step 2.1 a past causal segment from $p$ to $q$ is a null geodesic lying in the future boundary. Concatenate the past segment $\gamma|_{[0,b]}$ from $p_0$ to $p$ with this past segment from $p$ to $q$. If the two tangent rays at $p$ differ, the resulting corner and [L3] yield $q\ll p_0$, contradicting achronality [L2]. If they agree, rescale the second affine parameter by a positive constant to match the nonzero velocities at $p$. Uniqueness of the geodesic equation [L4] identifies a short initial portion of the second segment with $\gamma((b,b+\varepsilon])$, for some $0<\varepsilon<T-b$. That portion lies in $\partial U$ by step 2.1, contradicting step 3.1. Both alternatives are impossible. Thus $J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}$, with $p\in C\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ as required.

derivations.claim: (Setup.) Let $\gamma:[0,\varepsilon]\to M$ be a future timelike curve with $\gamma(0)=p$ (it exists since every point of a time-oriented Lorentzian manifold has a future timelike curve). If the conclusion failed for every $q=\gamma(t)$, there would be a sequence $t_j\in(0,\varepsilon]$ with $t_j\to0$ and points $q_j\in J^-(\gamma(t_j))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$.

(The correctly directed complement exclusion.) Suppose $r\in\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ and $r\le p$. Since $\Sigma\subset U$, $r\notin\Sigma$ and hence $r\in I^+(\Sigma)$. Choose a short past timelike perturbation $r_-\ll r$ inside the open set $\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. Push-up gives $r_-\ll r\le p$, so $I^+(r_-)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is an open neighborhood of the boundary point $p$. It meets $U$ at $s$. A timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $r_-$ followed by one from $r_-$ to $s\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ contradicts past convexity [L4], because it passes through $r_-\notin U$. Thus there is no such $r$. This uses a past perturbation; no future perturbation below a null-related endpoint is inferred.

(Compactness and a limit.) Fix any $t_\ast\in(0,\varepsilon]$ with $t_\ast\ge t_j$ for all $j$ (equivalently pass to the subsequence with $t_j\le\varepsilon$); then $q_j\in J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$ for all $j$. Since $U^c$ and $W^c$ are closed and $J^+(\Sigma)$ is closed [L1], the set $J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$ is closed in the compact set $J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ of [L2], hence compact; passing to a subsequence, $q_j\to q$ with $q\in J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$.
($q\le p$.) Since $q_j\le\gamma(t_j)$ for every $j$, $q_j\to q$ and $\gamma(t_j)\to p$, closedness of the causal relation [L1] gives $q\le p$.

($q=p$, hence $q\in W$, contradiction.) If $q\in\partial U$, then $q\in J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}$ by the exposed-point property, so $q=p\in W$, contradicting $q\in W^c$ of step 2.1. Hence $q\in U^c\setminus\partial U$; but $q\le p$ by step 3.1 and $q\in J^+(\Sigma)$ by step 2.1, contradicting step 1.2. Therefore the assumption of step 1.1 is false: for every sufficiently small $t$ one has $J^-(\gamma(t))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W$, which is the assertion with $q:=\gamma(t)$.

$0\le s\le t\le b_k$, with $\alpha_k(0)\to x\in M$ and
$\alpha_k(b_k)\to z\in M$. Passing to a subsequence, let
$b:=\lim_kb_k\in[0,\infty]$. Then:

**(i) Bounded case.** If $b<\infty$, there is a subsequence and a future causal
curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=x$, $\alpha(b)=z$ and
$d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le t-s$ for $s\le t$, such that the subsequence
converges to $\alpha$ uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,b]$ after the following
common-domain reparametrization when $b>0$:
$$\widetilde\alpha_k(t):=\alpha_k\!\left(\frac{b_k}{b}t\right),\qquad 0\le t\le b.$$
Thus $\widetilde\alpha_k(0)=\alpha_k(0)$ and
$\widetilde\alpha_k(b)=\alpha_k(b_k)$. If $b=0$, then $x=z$ and the curves
converge to the constant curve at $x$ uniformly on their varying domains in
the sense that $\sup_{0\le t\le b_k}d_h(\alpha_k(t),x)\to0$.

**(ii) Unbounded case.** If $b=\infty$, there are a future-inextendible future
causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$ and a
past-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with
$\alpha^-(0)=z$, such that a subsequence converges to $\alpha^+$ uniformly on
every compact subinterval of $[0,\infty)$ and to $\alpha^-$ uniformly on every
compact subinterval of $(-\infty,0]$ (where $\alpha^-$ is the limit of the
curves $s\mapsto\alpha_k(b_k+s)$, $s\le0$, for large $k$). Moreover for all
$t_+\ge0$ and $t_-\le0$ there are parameters $u_k\le v_k$ with
$u_k\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $v_k\to\alpha^-(t_-)$; in particular
$(\alpha^+(t_+),\alpha^-(t_-))$ lies in the closure of the causal relation in
the strong sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (c):
there exist sequences $u_j\le v_j$ with $u_j\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and
$v_j\to\alpha^-(t_-)$.

**(iii) Coincident endpoints.** If $x=z$, then in case (i) with $b>0$ the
curve $\alpha$ is a nonconstant closed future causal curve through $x$
($\alpha(0)=\alpha(b)=x$), and in case (ii) the concatenation $\gamma$ of
$\alpha^-$ and $\alpha^+$ is an inextendible future causal curve
$\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$ with $\gamma(0)=x$.

**(iv) Imprisonment.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be strongly causal
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (b)) and
suppose all images $\alpha_k([0,b_k])$ are contained in one compact set $K$.
Then $b\le L(K)<\infty$ where $L(K)$ is the length bound of
[[lem-gr-strong-causality-compact-length-bound]]; in particular the case
$b=\infty$ is excluded.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let $L_g$ be the Lorentzian
length functional of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]] on future
causal curves ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). For a strictly
convex normal ball $U$ ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) and
$p,q\in U$ put
$$d_U(p,q):=\sqrt{\max\bigl(0,-g_p(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q))\bigr)},$$
a continuous function of $(p,q)$ on $U\times U$
([[lem-gr-position-vector-differential]] clause (c)).

**(a) Refined sums.** Let $\alpha:[a,b]\to M$ be a future causal curve and
let $(\mathcal P_N)$ be a sequence of partitions
$a=t_0^N<t_1^N<\dots<t_{m_N}^N=b$ with mesh tending to zero such that every
subarc $\alpha([t_i^N,t_{i+1}^N])$ is contained in a strictly convex normal
ball $U_i^N$ (such partitions exist and may be obtained from any fixed finite
cover of $\alpha([a,b])$ by strictly convex normal balls and a Lebesgue-number
subdivision). Then
$$L_g(\alpha)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{i=0}^{m_N-1}d_{U_i^N}\bigl(\alpha(t_i^N),\alpha(t_{i+1}^N)\bigr).$$
In particular the limit is independent of the choice of the partitions and of
the balls $U_i^N$.

**(b) Upper semicontinuity.** Let $\alpha_k:[a,b]\to M$ be future causal
curves converging to $\alpha:[a,b]\to M$ uniformly on $[a,b]$ (in the manifold
topology, equivalently along any Riemannian distance). Then
$$\limsup_{k\to\infty}L_g(\alpha_k)\le L_g(\alpha).$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $C\subseteq M$ be a strictly
convex normal set ([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]]
clause (b)), let $p\in C$, and write
$$W_p:=\exp_p^{-1}(C)\subseteq T_pM,\qquad v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q),\qquad P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q)),\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q)).$$
Define
$$J_C^+(p):=\{p\}\cup\{q\in C:\text{there is a future causal curve } \sigma:[0,1]\to C\text{ with }\sigma(0)=p,\ \sigma(1)=q\},$$
so the reflexive endpoint $p$ is included even though a constant curve is
not in the curve class. Define
$$I_C^+(p):=\{q\in C:\text{there is a future timelike curve } \sigma:[0,1]\to C\text{ with }\sigma(0)=p,\ \sigma(1)=q\}$$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Put
$$\mathcal C^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future causal or }v=0\},\quad \mathcal T^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future timelike}\},\quad \mathcal N^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future null and }v\ne0\}.$$
Then:

**(a) Causal containment.** For every future causal curve
$\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ with $\sigma(0)=p$, the position vector
$v(\sigma(t))$ is future causal or zero for every $t\in[0,1]$.

**(b) Cone characterizations.**
$$J^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal C^+),\qquad I^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal T^+),\qquad J^+_C(p)\setminus\bigl(I^+_C(p)\cup\{p\}\bigr)=\exp_p(\mathcal N^+).$$

**(c) Null rigidity.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$, and let $\hat s\in(0,1]$ satisfy: $v(\sigma(\hat s))$ is
future null nonzero and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for every $t\in(0,\hat s]$. Then
there are $v_0\in\mathcal N^+$ and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous
surjection $\varphi:[0,\hat s]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for $0\le t\le\hat s$.

**(d) Length maximality.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$. Then
$$L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-D_p^2\bigl(\sigma(1)\bigr)}=\sqrt{-g_p\bigl(v(\sigma(1)),v(\sigma(1))\bigr)} .$$
If moreover $v(\sigma(1))$ is future timelike and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for all
$t\in(0,1]$, then equality holds if and only if there are $v_0$ future
timelike and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous surjection
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for all $t$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $p\in M$ and let
$U_p=\exp_p(W_p)$ be a normal neighborhood of $p$ as in
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (a). Let
$\sigma:[a,b]\to U_p$ be a future causal curve in the class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] (locally absolutely continuous,
with future causal nonzero velocity almost everywhere), and write
$$v(t):=\exp_p^{-1}\bigl(\sigma(t)\bigr),\qquad P(t):=d(\exp_p)_{v(t)}(v(t)),\qquad Q(t):=g_p(v(t),v(t))$$
for $t\in[a,b]$. Suppose there is $t^*\in[a,b]$ such that $v(t^*)$ is
future timelike. Then:

**(a) Propagation.** For every $t\in[t^*,b]$ with
$\sigma([t^*,t])\subseteq U_p$, the vector $v(t)$ is future timelike;
consequently $Q(t)<0$, and $R(t):=\sqrt{-Q(t)}>0$.

**(b) Length inequality.** For all $t^*\le t_1<t_2\le b$ with
$\sigma([t_1,t_2])\subseteq U_p$,
$$R(t_2)-R(t_1)\ \ge\ L_g\bigl(\sigma|_{[t_1,t_2]}\bigr),$$
the Lorentzian length of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]].
In particular $R$ is nondecreasing on $[t^*,b]$.

**(c) Derivative formula.** The map $t\mapsto Q(t)$ is absolutely
continuous and
$$\frac{d}{dt}Q(t)=2\,g_{\sigma(t)}\bigl(P(t),\sigma'(t)\bigr)$$
at almost every $t\in[a,b]$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), and let $\exp_q:\mathcal E_q\to M$
be the exponential maps of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. For an open set
$U\subseteq M$ write $T U\subseteq TM$ for the tangent vectors based at
points of $U$.

**(a) Normal neighborhood.** An open neighborhood $U$ of $p\in M$ is a
**normal neighborhood of $p$** when there is an open star-shaped subset
$W\subseteq\mathcal E_p$ of $T_pM$ such that $U=\exp_p(W)$ and
$\exp_p|_W:W\to U$ is a diffeomorphism onto $U$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clause (b)
supplies such pairs). The **exponential coordinates at $p$** on such a $U$
are $u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U\to\mathbb R^4$ for a linear isomorphism
$\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$.

**(b) Convex normal and strictly convex normal sets.** An open set
$C\subseteq M$ is **convex normal** when it is a normal neighborhood of each
of its points; thus for every $q\in C$ there is an open star-shaped
$C_q\subseteq\mathcal E_q$ with $\exp_q(C_q)=C$ and
$\exp_q|_{C_q}$ a diffeomorphism onto $C$. It is **strictly convex normal**
when every pair $q,q'\in\overline C$ is joined by exactly one affinely
parametrized geodesic segment $\gamma:[0,1]\to\overline C$ with
$\gamma(0)=q$ and $\gamma(1)=q'$, and, if $q\ne q'$, its parameter interior
$\gamma((0,1))$ lies in $C$. In the degenerate case $q=q'$, the required
segment is the constant geodesic at $q$; no interior-containment condition
is imposed on this degenerate segment when $q\in\partial C$.

**(c) Position vector.** Let $C$ be convex normal, let $p,q\in C$ and let
$x:[0,1]\to C$ be the unique geodesic with $x(0)=p$, $x(1)=q$ supplied by
the definition of strict convexity outside the endpoints; equivalently
$x(t)=\exp_p(t\,\exp_p^{-1}(q))$ for $t\in[0,1]$ and
$v:=\exp_p^{-1}(q)\in T_pM$. The vector
$$P(p,q):=\gamma_{p,v}'(1)=d(\exp_p)_{v}(v)\in T_qM$$
is the **position vector of $q$ with respect to $p$**; here
$\gamma_{p,v}$ is the maximal geodesic of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. By the Gauss lemma of
[[thm-gr-lorentz-gauss-lemma-and-normal-maximum]]
$g_q(P(p,q),P(p,q))=g_p(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q))$.

**(d) Squared-displacement function.** For a normal neighborhood $U$ of
$p$ the **squared-displacement function** is
$$D_p^2:U\to\mathbb R,\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p\bigl(\exp_p^{-1}(q),\exp_p^{-1}(q)\bigr).$$
It is smooth on $U$ because $\exp_p^{-1}$ is smooth and $g_p$ is bilinear;
$D_p^2(p)=0$, $D_p^2(q)<0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is timelike,
$D_p^2(q)=0$ exactly when $P(p,q)$ is null or zero, and $D_p^2(q)>0$
exactly when $P(p,q)$ is spacelike. On a convex normal $C$ we write
$D^2:C\times C\to\mathbb R$, $D^2(p,q):=D_p^2(q)$, whenever the position
vector is defined.

**(e) Scope.** These are definitions inside the smooth Lorentzian model;
they assert no existence of convex normal sets (supplied separately by
[[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]), no completeness and no physical
reading. The position vector is an element of $T_qM$, not a vector field and
not a coordinate displacement; $D^2$ is not a metric distance and takes
negative values on timelike-separated pairs.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
geodesics, their maximal domains $I_{q,v}$ and the exponential maps
$\exp_q$ be those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Fix
$p\in M$. Write $\pi:TM\to M$ for the bundle projection.

**(a) Smoothness of the joint map.** The set
$$\mathcal D:=\{(q,v)\in TM:\ 1\in I_{q,v}\}\subseteq TM$$
is open in $TM$, and the **joint exponential map**
$$\Phi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M\times M,\qquad \Phi(q,v):=(q,\exp_q v),$$
is smooth.

**(b) Differential at $(p,0)$.** The differential $d\Phi_{(p,0)}$ is an
isomorphism. Explicitly, fix a smooth chart $(U,x)$ around $p$; it induces
the chart $(TU,Tx)$ of $TM$ and the product chart $(U\times U,x\times x)$ of
$M\times M$, and under the induced identifications
$T_{(p,0)}(TM)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ and
$T_{(p,p)}(M\times M)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ one has
$$d\Phi_{(p,0)}(u,w)=(u,\ u+w)\qquad\text{for all }u,w\in T_pM .$$

**(c) Diffeomorphism and two-point inverse.** There are open neighborhoods
$V\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $(p,0)$ and $W\subseteq M\times M$ of $(p,p)$ such
that $\Phi|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Moreover $V$ can be chosen
product-like: there are a chart $(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$, a radius
$r>0$ and a velocity radius $\rho>0$ such that, writing $B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb
R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$,
$$V=\bigl\{(q,v):\ q\in x^{-1}(B_r),\ \text{the coordinate components of }v\text{ in }(TU,Tx)\text{ lie in }B_\rho\bigr\},$$
and there is $s\in(0,r)$ with $x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$.
Consequently the velocity map
$$v:W\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (q,r)\longmapsto v(q,r):=\text{the vector with }(q,v(q,r))\in V,\ \Phi(q,v(q,r))=(q,r),$$
is well defined and smooth, and $\exp_q\bigl(v(q,r)\bigr)=r$ for all
$(q,r)\in W$.

**(d) Lipschitz bound for the two-point inverse.** On every pair
$x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$ as in (c) there is a constant
$\Lambda\ge 0$ such that, for all $q,r\in x^{-1}(B_s)$,
$$|v(q,r)|_x\le\Lambda\,\bigl|x(q)-x(r)\bigr|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $|v|_x$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate components of
$v$ and $v(q,q)=0$. In particular $|v(q,r)|_x\le 2\Lambda s$ on this pair.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.

3. **Geodesic speed and proper time.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the function
   $t\mapsto g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))$ is constant. If $\gamma$
   is nonconstant, its tangent is nowhere zero and its causal character
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant; a constant geodesic has zero
   tangent and is assigned none of those causal characters. If $\gamma$ is a
   **future-directed timelike geodesic** and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then for
   $t_0<t_1$ its proper-time increment over $[t_0,t_1]$ is
   $\lambda(t_1-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter. In this parameter its four-velocity is
   $U=(c/\lambda)\gamma'$ and is parallel: $D_\tau U=0$. Proper time is not
   assigned to a past-directed curve by that definition; reversing the
   parameter gives a future-directed timelike geodesic with the same
   (positive) proper-time magnitude. A nonconstant null geodesic has null
   tangent and admits no proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic whose
   tangent is nowhere zero, and let $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto
   its open image with $h'\neq0$. Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and
   only if $h(s)=as+b$ with constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the
   constant $h'$, and every affine parameter of this nonconstant geodesic
   arises in this way from a fixed one. If $\gamma$ is constant, then
   $\gamma\circ h$ is constant and hence geodesic for every such $h$; no
   affine restriction on $h$ follows.

derivations.claim: (Finiteness.) Let $r\in J^-(q)$ and let $\alpha$ be any future causal curve from $r$ to $q$. Every point of $\alpha$ lies in $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$, which is compact, so by [L1] the $h$-arclength of $\alpha$ and hence $L_g(\alpha)$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $r,q$; therefore $\tau_q(r)<\infty$. If $r\notin J^-(q)$ no such curve exists and $\tau_q(r)=0$; if $r=q$ causality excludes a nonconstant return curve and the stipulated zero-separation convention gives $\tau_q(q)=0$, represented by the constant degenerate geodesic as specified in (a); and $\tau_q(r)>0$ iff there is a future timelike curve from $r$ to $q$, i.e. $r\in I^-(q)$.

(Attainment and geodesy of maximizers.) Let $r\in J^-(q)\setminus\{q\}$ and, using Countable Choice, let $\alpha_n$ be causal curves from $r$ to $q$ with $L_g(\alpha_n)\to\tau_q(r)$. All images lie in the compact set $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$; parametrize them by $h$-arclength as $\alpha_n:[0,b_n]\to M$. [step 1.1, L2, L3, L4, contradiction]
After a subsequence $b_n\to b<\infty$ by [L1], and $b\ge d_h(r,q)>0$.
The bounded two-endpoint theorem [L2] gives a joining limit
$\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ and uniform convergence of the actual normalized
causal representatives $\widetilde\alpha_n(t):=\alpha_n((b_n/b)t)$ on
$[0,b]$. Set $\beta_n(s):=\widetilde\alpha_n(bs)=\alpha_n(b_ns)$ and
$\beta(s):=\alpha(bs)$ on $[0,1]$; their uniform convergence is exactly
that of the supplied representatives after the fixed parameter change.
The $\beta_n$ and $\beta$ are causal curves on a single fixed domain;
increasing affine reparametrization preserves Lorentzian length.
Thus [L2]'s length semicontinuity applies to these curves, and, with
$\gamma:=\beta$, gives $L_g(\gamma)\ge\limsup L_g(\alpha_n)=\tau_q(r)$, so $L_g(\gamma)=\tau_q(r)$. In every sufficiently small convex normal neighborhood, the local Lorentzian normal-maximum theorem [L3] bounds the length of a subarc by that of its radial causal geodesic, with equality only along that geodesic up to increasing reparametrization. If any subarc failed this equality condition, finite replacement would strictly increase the total length, contradicting maximality. Thus all local subarcs have geodesic images; on overlaps they have the same tangent ray and geodesic uniqueness joins them into a single causal geodesic up to monotone reparametrization, and its image lies in $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$.

(The radial formula.) Let $V,W,q$ be as in clause (b) and let $r\in W\cap I^-(q)$. Let $\gamma$ be a maximizer from $r$ to $q$ (step 2.1). Since $W$ is causally convex, $\gamma\subseteq W\subseteq V$; by [L3] applied in $V$ with base point $q$, every causal curve in $V$ from $r$ to $q$ has length at most $\sqrt{-g_q(\exp_q^{-1}(r),\exp_q^{-1}(r))}$, with equality exactly for the radial geodesic, which lies in $V$; since all competitors from $r$ to $q$ lie in $W\subseteq V$ and the radial segment itself is a competitor with that length, $\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{-g_q(\exp_q^{-1}(r),\exp_q^{-1}(r))}$. The right-hand side is smooth on $I^-(q)\cap W$ by [L3] and the smoothness of the inverse exponential map; its continuous extension by $0$ at points of $W\setminus J^-(q)$ and at $q$ is exactly $\tau_q$ there by step 1.1.

(Upper semicontinuity on compact sets.) Let $r_n\to r$ in a compact $K$. If $\limsup\tau_q(r_n)=0$, upper semicontinuity is immediate from nonnegativity. Otherwise take a subsequence approaching that positive limsup; discard zero-separation terms, so every remaining $r_n\ne q$ is causally related to $q$. Choose, by Countable Choice, $\alpha_n$ be causal curves from $r_n$ to $q$ with $L_g(\alpha_n)\ge\tau_q(r_n)-1/n$. Passing to the compact diamond $J^+(K')\cap J^-(q)$ for a compact $K'$ containing the $r_n$ ([L1]), parametrize $\alpha_n:[0,b_n]\to M$ by $h$-arclength and pass to [step 2.1, L1, L2, algebra]
$b_n\to b<\infty$ using [L1]. The case $b=0$ cannot occur on this
positive-limsup subsequence: the compact-set metric comparison gives
$L_g(\alpha_n)\le Cb_n\to0$, contradicting
$L_g(\alpha_n)\ge\tau_q(r_n)-1/n$.
For $b>0$ the bounded two-endpoint limit gives $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$.
As in step 2.1, the actual causal curves $\beta_n(s)=\alpha_n(b_ns)$
converge uniformly on $[0,1]$ to $\gamma(s)=\alpha(bs)$, and retain exactly
the original Lorentzian lengths. Hence the common-domain length theorem
applies, giving $\limsup_n\tau_q(r_n)\le\limsup_nL_g(\alpha_n)\le L_g(\gamma)\le\tau_q(r)$ by upper semicontinuity [L2] and step 2.1. If $r\in I^-(q)$ then a maximizer $\gamma_r$ from $r$ to $q$ exists (step 2.1); since $I^-(q)$ is open, for $n$ large the inner segment of $\gamma_r$ can be joined to $r_n$ by a short timelike segment inside $I^-(q)$, giving $\liminf_n\tau_q(r_n)\ge\tau_q(r)$ by letting the inner cut shrink; combined with the upper bound this gives continuity at $r$.
