For the absolutely continuous curve conclusion (c), assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) as required by the cited causal-curve calculus and fundamental theorem. The other clauses use the given smooth observer structure, pointwise adapted-chart existence and finite compactness arguments, without these additional curve-calculus premises. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), and put $n=N/\sqrt{-g(N,N)}$. Write $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. In a chart $(U,x)$ put $v^a=dx^a(v)$, $v_s=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and $|v|_{\mathrm e}=(\sum_{a=0}^3(v^a)^2)^{1/2}$.

**(a) Adapted orthonormal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there are a chart $(U,x)$, $x(p)=0$, a radius $r>0$ with $U=x^{-1}(B_r)$, and $K\ge1$, such that on all of $U$
$$n=\partial_{x^0},\qquad g_{00}\equiv-1,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}.$$

**(b) Cone domination.** The chart and radius in (a) can be chosen so every nonzero future causal vector at any point of $U$ satisfies
$$|v_s|\le K v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le K v^0\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad v^0\ge K^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$

**(c) Curve form.** Every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] has strictly increasing time coordinate, and for all $s<t$ in $I$
$$x^0(\gamma(s))<x^0(\gamma(t)),\qquad |x_s(\gamma(t))-x_s(\gamma(s))|\le K\left(x^0(\gamma(t))-x^0(\gamma(s))\right).$$
Consequently every spatial component satisfies the same bound, and the curve image is the graph of a $K$-Lipschitz function into Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ over the interval $x^0(\gamma(I))$.

**(d) Flat minorant cone.** The same chart can be chosen so the constant-coordinate metric $\eta_{16}=-(dx^0)^2+16\sum_i(dx^i)^2$ has every nonzero $\eta_{16}$-causal vector $g$-timelike throughout $U$. If $q,q'\in U$ and $\eta_{16}(x(q')-x(q),x(q')-x(q))<0$, then $q\ll q'$ if $x^0(q')>x^0(q)$, and $q'\ll q$ otherwise.

**(e) General temporal charts: exact compact uniformity.** For any chart $(U',z)$ define its temporal locus
$$P=\{q\in U':\nabla z^0(q)\text{ is past timelike}\}.$$
For every compact set $K_0\subset P$ there is $L\ge1$ such that all nonzero future causal vectors based in $K_0$, with coordinate components and Euclidean norm taken in $z$, satisfy
$$|v_s|\le L v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le L v^0,\qquad v^0\ge L^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$
In particular these bounds hold throughout any relatively compact $U_0\Subset U'$ whose closure is contained in $P$, equivalently whose time gradient is past timelike on its entire closure. Timelikeness merely on $U_0$ gives local bounds at each point and uniform bounds on each compact subset of $U_0$; it does not alone give a uniform bound on all of $U_0$.

No additional choice is used to select the pointwise linear bases or compact cone constants. Countable and Dependent Choice are explicitly required only for the general absolutely continuous curve clause (c), through its actual calculus suppliers.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, with the
relations $\ll$, $\le$ and the sets $I^\pm$, $J^\pm$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] and the future and past sets of
[[def-gr-future-and-past-sets]]. Then:

**(a) Openness.** For every $x\in M$ the chronological future $I^+(x)$ and
the chronological past $I^-(x)$ are open subsets of $M$.

**(b) The chronological relation is open.** The set
$$\{(x,y)\in M\times M:\ x\ll y\}$$
is open in the product topology of $M\times M$.

**(c) Closure of future and past sets.** Let $F\subseteq M$ be a future set,
that is $I^+(F)\subseteq F$. Then every $q\in\overline F$ satisfies
$I^+(q)\subseteq F$. Dually, if $P$ is a past set ($I^-(P)\subseteq P$) and
$q\in\overline P$, then $I^-(q)\subseteq P$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ and the relations $\ll$, $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Then:

**(a)** if $p\ll q$ and $q\le r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(b)** if $p\le q$ and $q\ll r$, then $p\ll r$;

**(c)** if $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ is a future causal curve and there are
$a\le s<t\le b$ such that $\gamma|_{[s,t]}$ is a future timelike curve, then
$\gamma(a)\ll\gamma(b)$;

**(d)** consequently
$$I^+\bigl(J^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega),\qquad I^-\bigl(J^-(\Omega)\bigr)=I^-(\Omega)$$
for every $\Omega\subseteq M$, and dually
$J^+\bigl(I^+(\Omega)\bigr)=I^+(\Omega)$.

No choice principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}}\quad\text{(pointwise)},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat,$$
with the flat map $\flat$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
so that $h$ is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Then:

**(a)** $h$ is a smooth Riemannian (positive definite) metric on $M$.

**(b)** There is a smooth nonnegative proper function $f:M\to[0,\infty)$ such
that the metric
$$h':=(1+|df|_h^2)\,h$$
is a smooth Riemannian metric with $|df|_{h'}\le1$ everywhere.

**(c)** For each connected component $M_0$ of $M$, the metric space
$(M_0,d_{h'})$ is complete, where $d_{h'}$ is the Riemannian distance of
$h'|_{M_0}$ ([[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]],
[[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]]).

**(d)** Consequently, for every connected component $M_0$, every subset of
$M_0$ that is closed in $M_0$ and bounded in $d_{h'}$ is compact, and every
closed ball $\{q\in M_0:d_{h'}(q,p)\le r\}$ is compact.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $h$ be a smooth positive
definite metric on $M$ such that $(M,d_h)$ is complete in each connected
component and every closed $d_h$-bounded subset is compact (both hold for the
metric $h'$ of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]).

**(a) Compact parameter intervals.** Let $T>0$ and let
$\alpha_k:[0,T]\to M$ be future causal curves
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]) parametrized by $h$-arclength,
$\ell_h(\alpha_k|_{[s,t]})=t-s$ for all $0\le s\le t\le T$, with
$\alpha_k(0)\to p\in M$. Then some subsequence (still written $\alpha_k$)
converges uniformly in $d_h$ on $[0,T]$ to a map
$\alpha:[0,T]\to M$ with:

**(a1)** $\alpha(0)=p$ and $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le|t-s|$ for all
$s,t\in[0,T]$;

**(a2)** $\alpha$ is a geodesically connectible continuous causal curve in
the sense of [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]];

**(a3)** $\alpha$ is a future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]; and for every chart $U$ of the
kind produced by [[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (b), with
domination constant $K$ and time coordinate $x^0$, there is a constant
$C\ge1$, depending only on the chart and $h$, such that
$$t-s\le C\bigl(x^0(\alpha(t))-x^0(\alpha(s))\bigr)$$
whenever $s<t$ and $\alpha([s,t])\subseteq U$;

**(a4)** $\alpha$ is not constant on any nondegenerate parameter interval.

**(b) Half-lines.** Let $\gamma_k:I_k\to M$ be future causal curves
parametrized by $h$-arclength whose intervals $I_k\ni0$ satisfy
$[0,n]\subseteq I_k$ for every $k$ once $n$ is fixed (for instance
$I_k=[0,b_k]$ with $b_k\to\infty$), and suppose $\gamma_k(0)\to p$. Then
some subsequence converges uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of
$[0,\infty)$ to a future causal curve $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ satisfying
(a1)-(a4) on compact subintervals and which is future-inextendible
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)). A dual statement
holds, in the time-reversed orientation, for curves whose intervals satisfy
$[-n,0]\subseteq I_k$ eventually; it produces a past-inextendible future
causal curve on $(-\infty,0]$ in the original orientation.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with the causal-curve class of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Chart independence.** Local absolute continuity in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (a) is independent of the
chosen chart and of the smooth atlas: if one chart representative of a curve
is absolutely continuous on every compact parameter subinterval, then so is
every other one.

**(b) Velocity and smooth composition.** At every interior parameter value
$t$ at which one chart representative is differentiable, every chart
representative is differentiable, the velocity $\gamma'(t)$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (b) is well defined and
independent of the chart, and the set of parameter values at which some
chart representative is differentiable has full measure in the domain. For
every smooth map $F$ of an open subset of $M$ into $M$ whose domain contains
the image of $\gamma$, the composite $F\circ\gamma$ is locally absolutely
continuous and $(F\circ\gamma)'(t)=dF_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t))$ at almost
every parameter value $t$.

**(c) Piecewise $C^1$ curves.** Every piecewise $C^1$ curve (with the finite
admissible partition and one-sided endpoint convention of clause (a) of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]) is locally absolutely
continuous; a piecewise $C^1$ curve all of whose tangents are future causal
is a future causal curve, and if in addition its tangents are future
timelike, it is a future timelike curve.

**(d) Concatenation.** If $\gamma_1:[a,b]\to M$ and $\gamma_2:[b,c]\to M$ are
future causal curves (respectively future timelike curves) with
$\gamma_1(b)=\gamma_2(b)$, then the concatenation $\gamma:[a,c]\to M$,
$\gamma(t):=\gamma_1(t)$ for $t\le b$ and $\gamma(t):=\gamma_2(t)$ for
$t\ge b$, is a future causal (respectively future timelike) curve; the same
holds for any finite chain of such curves.

**(e) Reparametrization.** If $\varphi:J\to I$ is a strictly increasing
$C^1$ diffeomorphism of intervals with $\varphi'>0$ and $\gamma:I\to M$ is
locally absolutely continuous, then $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is locally
absolutely continuous and $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is future causal (respectively
future timelike) exactly when $\gamma$ is. Moreover $\gamma$ is
future-inextendible if and only if $\gamma\circ\varphi$ is
future-inextendible, and this equivalence holds for every strictly increasing
continuous surjection $\varphi$ of intervals, not only the $C^1$ ones.

**(f) Relations.** The relation $\le$ of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is reflexive and transitive, and
$p\ll q$ implies $p\le q$ for all $p,q$; the relations $J^{\pm}$ and
$I^{\pm}$ of that definition are therefore nested, $I^{\pm}(S)\subseteq
J^{\pm}(S)$ for every $S\subseteq M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]) and geodesics as in
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$O\subseteq M$ be an open neighborhood of $p$. Then there are a chart
$(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and a radius $r>0$ such that
$C:=x^{-1}(B_r)$, $B_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<r\}$ based at
$0=x(p)$, is contained in $O$ and has the following properties.

**(a) Normal neighborhood of each point.** For every $q\in C$ define
$$W_q:=\bigl\{u\in\mathcal E_q:\ \exp_q(tu)\in C\ \text{for every }t\in[0,1]\bigr\},$$
where $\mathcal E_q$ is the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (d). Then $W_q$ is an
open star-shaped neighborhood of $0$ in $T_qM$, and
$\exp_q|_{W_q}:W_q\to C$ is a diffeomorphism onto $C$.

**(b) Unique contained joining segment.** For all $q,q'\in C$ there is
exactly one geodesic segment joining $q$ to $q'$ whose image is contained in
$C$, namely
$$x_{q,q'}:[0,1]\to C,\qquad x_{q,q'}(t)=\exp_q\bigl(t\,v(q,q')\bigr),$$
where $v(q,q')$ is the two-point inverse velocity of
[[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]] clause (c). For $q\ne q'$ the
points $x_{q,q'}(t)$, $0<t<1$, lie in $C$ strictly inside the coordinate
ball, i.e. $|x(x_{q,q'}(t))|_{\mathrm e}<r$; and $x_{q',q}$ is the time
reverse of $x_{q,q'}$ up to affine reparametrization.

**(c) Strict convexity.** In the terminology of
[[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b), $C$ is a
strictly convex normal neighborhood; in particular the position vector
$P(q,q')=d(\exp_q)_{v(q,q')}\bigl(v(q,q')\bigr)$ and the squared
displacement $D^2(q,q')=g_q\bigl(v(q,q'),v(q,q')\bigr)$ are defined for all
$q,q'\in C$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). Let $C\subseteq M$ be a strictly
convex normal set ([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]]
clause (b)), let $p\in C$, and write
$$W_p:=\exp_p^{-1}(C)\subseteq T_pM,\qquad v(q):=\exp_p^{-1}(q),\qquad P(p,q):=d(\exp_p)_{v(q)}(v(q)),\qquad D_p^2(q):=g_p(v(q),v(q)).$$
Define
$$J_C^+(p):=\{p\}\cup\{q\in C:\text{there is a future causal curve } \sigma:[0,1]\to C\text{ with }\sigma(0)=p,\ \sigma(1)=q\},$$
so the reflexive endpoint $p$ is included even though a constant curve is
not in the curve class. Define
$$I_C^+(p):=\{q\in C:\text{there is a future timelike curve } \sigma:[0,1]\to C\text{ with }\sigma(0)=p,\ \sigma(1)=q\}$$
([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Put
$$\mathcal C^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future causal or }v=0\},\quad \mathcal T^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future timelike}\},\quad \mathcal N^+:=\{v\in W_p:v\text{ is future null and }v\ne0\}.$$
Then:

**(a) Causal containment.** For every future causal curve
$\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ with $\sigma(0)=p$, the position vector
$v(\sigma(t))$ is future causal or zero for every $t\in[0,1]$.

**(b) Cone characterizations.**
$$J^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal C^+),\qquad I^+_C(p)=\exp_p(\mathcal T^+),\qquad J^+_C(p)\setminus\bigl(I^+_C(p)\cup\{p\}\bigr)=\exp_p(\mathcal N^+).$$

**(c) Null rigidity.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$, and let $\hat s\in(0,1]$ satisfy: $v(\sigma(\hat s))$ is
future null nonzero and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for every $t\in(0,\hat s]$. Then
there are $v_0\in\mathcal N^+$ and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous
surjection $\varphi:[0,\hat s]\to[0,1]$ with
$\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for $0\le t\le\hat s$.

**(d) Length maximality.** Let $\sigma:[0,1]\to C$ be future causal with
$\sigma(0)=p$. Then
$$L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-D_p^2\bigl(\sigma(1)\bigr)}=\sqrt{-g_p\bigl(v(\sigma(1)),v(\sigma(1))\bigr)} .$$
If moreover $v(\sigma(1))$ is future timelike and $v(\sigma(t))\ne0$ for all
$t\in(0,1]$, then equality holds if and only if there are $v_0$ future
timelike and a nondecreasing absolutely continuous surjection
$\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ with $\sigma(t)=\exp_p(\varphi(t)v_0)$ for all $t$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
geodesics, their maximal domains $I_{q,v}$ and the exponential maps
$\exp_q$ be those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Fix
$p\in M$. Write $\pi:TM\to M$ for the bundle projection.

**(a) Smoothness of the joint map.** The set
$$\mathcal D:=\{(q,v)\in TM:\ 1\in I_{q,v}\}\subseteq TM$$
is open in $TM$, and the **joint exponential map**
$$\Phi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M\times M,\qquad \Phi(q,v):=(q,\exp_q v),$$
is smooth.

**(b) Differential at $(p,0)$.** The differential $d\Phi_{(p,0)}$ is an
isomorphism. Explicitly, fix a smooth chart $(U,x)$ around $p$; it induces
the chart $(TU,Tx)$ of $TM$ and the product chart $(U\times U,x\times x)$ of
$M\times M$, and under the induced identifications
$T_{(p,0)}(TM)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ and
$T_{(p,p)}(M\times M)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ one has
$$d\Phi_{(p,0)}(u,w)=(u,\ u+w)\qquad\text{for all }u,w\in T_pM .$$

**(c) Diffeomorphism and two-point inverse.** There are open neighborhoods
$V\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $(p,0)$ and $W\subseteq M\times M$ of $(p,p)$ such
that $\Phi|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Moreover $V$ can be chosen
product-like: there are a chart $(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$, a radius
$r>0$ and a velocity radius $\rho>0$ such that, writing $B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb
R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$,
$$V=\bigl\{(q,v):\ q\in x^{-1}(B_r),\ \text{the coordinate components of }v\text{ in }(TU,Tx)\text{ lie in }B_\rho\bigr\},$$
and there is $s\in(0,r)$ with $x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$.
Consequently the velocity map
$$v:W\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (q,r)\longmapsto v(q,r):=\text{the vector with }(q,v(q,r))\in V,\ \Phi(q,v(q,r))=(q,r),$$
is well defined and smooth, and $\exp_q\bigl(v(q,r)\bigr)=r$ for all
$(q,r)\in W$.

**(d) Lipschitz bound for the two-point inverse.** On every pair
$x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$ as in (c) there is a constant
$\Lambda\ge 0$ such that, for all $q,r\in x^{-1}(B_s)$,
$$|v(q,r)|_x\le\Lambda\,\bigl|x(q)-x(r)\bigr|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $|v|_x$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate components of
$v$ and $v(q,q)=0$. In particular $|v(q,r)|_x\le 2\Lambda s$ on this pair.

derivations.claim: Fix $s\in S$. There is no timelike loop through $s$: if $s\ll s$, openness gives $s\ll s'$ for all $s'\in S$ sufficiently near $s$, and the topological hypersurface has points $s'\ne s$ arbitrarily near $s$, contrary to acausality. Thus no two points of $S$, equal or distinct, are chronologically related. In particular $I^+(S)$ and $I^-(S)$ are disjoint by push-up.

We explain the arclength use in [L2]. For an avoiding one-sided causal curve, restrict to the half ending at the prescribed point. Its $h$-speed is locally integrable and positive almost everywhere, so its accumulated $h$-length is continuous strictly increasing. The inverse parameter gives a curve which is $1$-Lipschitz for $d_h$, because distance is at most original subcurve length; hence it is locally Lipschitz in charts. To verify the tangent and the arclength identity without assuming absolute continuity of the inverse parameter, let $\lambda(t)$ denote accumulated length. At almost every original parameter, both the chart curve and $\lambda$ are differentiable and $\lambda'(t)=\sqrt{h(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}>0$. Their exceptional set has measure zero. An absolutely continuous real function sends a measure-zero set to a measure-zero set: cover that set by intervals of arbitrarily small total length and apply the defining AC modulus to bound the total lengths of their image intervals. Thus its image under $\lambda$ is null, locally and hence on a countable exhaustion. At each remaining new parameter $u=\lambda(t)$, the inverse difference quotient is $1/\lambda'(t)$, and the chain difference quotient of the reparametrized chart curve is $\gamma'(t)/\lambda'(t)$. It is nonzero future causal and has $h$-norm one. This proves both admissibility and $h$-arclength parametrization. If the available one-sided length were finite, the $1$-Lipschitz curve would be Cauchy at that end and completeness would give a point limit, contrary to inextendibility. Thus these reparametrizations have full half-line domains, as required by [L2]. This argument changes parameters and never asserts an extension preserving an arbitrary original parameter.

Edgelessness supplies an open neighborhood $O$ of $s$ in which every timelike curve from $I^-_O(s)$ to $I^+_O(s)$ meets $S$. Take a temporal coordinate box $B=(-a,a)\times B_\rho$ with closure in $O$, centered at $s$. First choose $a>0$ small, and then $\rho>0$ small enough that all points $(-a,z)$ and $(a,z)$ belong respectively to $I^-_O(s)$ and $I^+_O(s)$; the narrower constant cone of [L1] ensures this. Every vertical segment between these endpoints therefore meets $S$, and has only one meeting by step 1.1. Write it $(f(z),z)$. The same narrower cone implies $|f(z)-f(z')|\le C|z-z'|$: otherwise the two graph points are joined by a timelike straight segment in $O$, contrary to step 1.1. Consequently $S\cap B$ is exactly a continuous Lipschitz graph; the sign of $t-f(z)$ separates the box into two open sides. A point above the graph belongs to $I^+(S)$ by its vertical segment; a point below belongs to $I^-(S)$.

A future causal segment starting at $s$ and remaining in this box cannot have an endpoint $q$ below the graph: the vertical segment from $q$ to the graph point $r$ gives $s\le q\ll r$, so $s\ll r$, excluded by step 1.1. If $q\in S$ and $q\ne s$, acausality excludes it. If $q=s$ but the segment is nondegenerate, choose an intermediate point $q'$ different from $s$ sufficiently near its start; it cannot lie below the graph or on $S$, so lies above it. Its vertical predecessor $r'\in S$ satisfies $r'\ll q'\le s$, again excluded by step 1.1. The same argument applies even if the rest of the loop leaves the box. Thus no nondegenerate causal loop passes through $S$, no causal curve meets $S$ twice, and every sufficiently short future segment from $S$ lies strictly above its local graph. Reversing time puts short past segments strictly below. Every causal curve through $s$ therefore crosses its local graph, and uniform approximations of a sufficiently short compact crossing segment also meet that graph by continuity of $t-f(z)$ and the intermediate value theorem.

If $q\in J^+(S)\setminus S$, take a causal curve $s\to q$ and a point $r$ on a sufficiently short initial segment. Step 3.1 puts $r$ above the graph. Its vertical predecessor $u\in S$ gives $u\ll r\le q$, hence $q\in I^+(S)$. Dually $J^-(S)\setminus S\subset I^-(S)$. For $p\in D^+(S)\setminus S$, the past half of the maximal timelike geodesic through $p$ is past-inextendible by [L3], and hence meets $S$; its timelike segment from that meeting to $p$ puts $p\in I^+(S)$. The dual argument proves the past-side inclusion. Also $S\subset D^+(S)\cap D^-(S)$ immediately.

Let $p\in D^+(S)\setminus S$. If $p$ were not interior to $D^+(S)$, choose $p_k\notin D^+(S)$ converging to $p$ and past-inextendible curves ending at $p_k$ and avoiding $S$. Step 1.2 and [L2] give a past-inextendible causal limit $\alpha:(-\infty,0]\to W$ with $\alpha(0)=p$. It meets $S$ at a negative parameter, by $p\in D^+(S)$ and $p\notin S$. By step 3.1 a short compact segment around that meeting crosses the local graph strictly. Uniform convergence on that segment forces the avoiding approximants to meet $S$, contradiction. Therefore $D^+(S)\setminus S$ is open; time reversal gives the dual result.

Let $s\in S$. If $s$ were not interior to $D(S)$, take $p_k\notin D(S)$ converging to $s$. At each $p_k$ choose a past-inextendible avoiding half and a future-inextendible avoiding half, concatenate them, and use step 1.2 to parametrize the two halves by signed arclength with $p_k$ at zero. Apply [L2] first to their past halves and then to the future halves of that subsequence. The two limits join at $s$ to an inextendible causal curve, and the common subsequence converges uniformly on each compact interval of the joined domain. Its short crossing segment through $s$ from step 3.1 forces the avoiding curves to meet $S$, contradiction. Thus $S\subset\operatorname{Int}D(S)$; together with step 4.2 and step 4.1 this proves (a).

A causal segment whose endpoints belong to $D^+(S)$ stays in $D^+(S)$. Indeed, if an intermediate $r$ were outside $D^+(S)$, a past-inextendible avoiding half ending at $r$ concatenated with the remaining segment $r\to q\in D^+(S)$ forces that remaining segment to meet $S$ at $u$. The initial endpoint $p\in D^+(S)$ belongs to $S\cup I^+(S)$ by step 4.1, whereas $p\le u$ puts $p\in S\cup I^-(S)$ by the dual of that step. Disjointness forces $p\in S$, and then the nondegenerate segment $p\to r\to u$ meets $S$ twice, excluded by step 3.1. This is a contradiction. The time reverse proves causal convexity of $D^-(S)$.

For a segment $p\to q$ in the remaining mixed case $p\in D^-(S)$, $q\in D^+(S)$, an intermediate $r\notin D(S)$ has both past- and future-inextendible avoiding halves. Concatenating the past half with $r\to q$ forces a meeting of $S$ strictly after $r$, and concatenating $p\to r$ with the future half forces a meeting strictly before $r$. This contradicts step 3.1. The opposite mixed case $p\in D^+(S)$, $q\in D^-(S)$ is impossible for a nondegenerate segment: step 4.1 yields $p\in S\cup I^+(S)$, $q\in S\cup I^-(S)$; if either endpoint is outside $S$, push-up gives a chronological relation between points of $S$, excluded by step 1.1, and if both are in $S$, step 3.1 excludes the segment. Along with step 5.2 this proves (b).

Let $\gamma:I\to D(S)$ be inextendible there and avoid $S$. Step 4.1 and connectedness of its image put it entirely in one of the disjoint open sets $I^+(S)$ and $I^-(S)$. Take the latter case; the other reverses time. Then every value belongs to $D^-(S)$. Fix $t_0\in I$. If the future half from $t_0$ has no point limit in $W$, that half is future-inextendible in $W$ and avoids $S$, contradicting $\gamma(t_0)\in D^-(S)$. Therefore the future end converges to some $y\in W$. If $y\in S$, then $y\in D(S)$ contradicts inextendibility in $D(S)$.

Suppose $y\notin S$ and $y\notin D^-(S)$. There is a future-inextendible avoiding half starting at $y$. A causal closed segment from $\gamma(t_0)$ to $y$ can be obtained as follows: use a smooth increasing diffeomorphism to reparametrize the future half of $\gamma$ to a finite interval with excluded upper end; this preserves local absolute continuity on its interior, and the endpoint-extension assertion of [L3] adjoins its limit $y$ as a causal endpoint. The resulting closed segment avoids $S$, including its endpoint. Concatenate it with the avoiding half from $y$. It is future-inextendible in $W$, avoids $S$, and starts at $\gamma(t_0)\in D^-(S)$, contradiction. Hence $y\in D^-(S)\subset D(S)$, which again contradicts inextendibility of $\gamma$ in the open submanifold. Every such curve therefore meets $S$, and step 3.1 supplies uniqueness of the parameter visit. This proves (c).

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data and
let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$C\subseteq\partial U$ be the set of boundary points that have a corresponding
point (clause (c) of that definition), and write $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$. If
$C\cap J^+(\Sigma)\neq\varnothing$, then there exists $p\in C\cap J^+(\Sigma)$
with
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed
boundary point in the sense of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]:
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$
Fix a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $p$
([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let
$p_1\ll p\ll p_2$ be points of $C$ such that $W:=I^+(p_1)\cap I^-(p_2)$
satisfies $\overline W\subseteq C$ (possible: strong causality at $p$ supplies
a neighbourhood $V_2\subseteq C$ of $p$ such that every causal curve with
both endpoints in $V_2$ is contained in $C$, and then
$\overline W\subseteq J^+(p_1)\cap J^-(p_2)\subseteq C$ for $p_1,p_2\in V_2$
by the same argument). Then $W$ is open, causally convex, $p\in W$, and
$\overline W$ is compact. Let $q\in W\cap I^+(p)$ be a point with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W,$$
chosen so close to $p$ along a future timelike curve that also $q\in W$
([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from
$q$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) and put
$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$
Let $W^\circ:=W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and let $S$ be the connected component of
the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in
$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(b)** $S$ is a nonempty smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface of $M$
without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap
C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(c)** There is a smooth positive function $\delta:S\to(0,\infty)$ with the
following properties. Define $X:=\nabla\tau_q/g(\nabla\tau_q,\nabla\tau_q)$
(so that $d\tau_q(X)=1$) on $\{\tau_q>0\}\cap W$, let $\phi_t$ be its local
flow, and put
$$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M,\qquad F(s,t):=\phi_t(s),\qquad N:=F\bigl(S\times(-\delta,\delta)\bigr).$$
Then $F$ is well defined and smooth, $N\subseteq W$ is open,
$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to N$ is a diffeomorphism,
$\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$, and:

1. every causal curve in $N$ is, in the coordinates $(s,t)$, of the form
   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric
   of $S$, and it meets $S$ in at most one parameter value;
2. every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets
   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;
3. for every $y\in N\cap U$ there is a unique $s\in S$ with $y=F(s,t_y)$, and the **punctured radial segment**
$$\{F(s,u):u\text{ between }0\text{ and }t_y,\ u\ne0\}$$
is contained in $U$. The base belongs to $U\cup C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, and the full segment including the base is contained in $U$ whenever $s\in U$. In particular, if $t_y<0$ then also $s\in U$. If $\Theta:N\to M'$ is a time-orientation-preserving local isometry with $\Theta|_S=\Phi|_S$, where $\Phi$ is the smooth extension of the common-subdevelopment map $\varphi$, then $\Theta=\varphi$ on $N\cap U$;
4. the tube can be chosen inside any prescribed open neighbourhood $O\subseteq W$ of the whole $S$, and below any prescribed positive continuous width ceiling on $S$. More quantitatively, write $q_0=g|_{TS}$ and $q_t=F_t^*g|_{TS}$. The construction gives $0<\delta<\tau_0/8$, $q_t\ge\tfrac12q_0$ for $|t|<\delta(s)$ and $|d\delta|_{q_0}\le1/(8\sqrt2)$. Every smooth positive smaller width $\widetilde\delta\le\delta$ satisfying $|d\widetilde\delta|_{q_0}\le1/(4\sqrt2)$ retains conclusions 1-3.

No compactness of $S$ or positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is assumed. The radial segment in clause 3 excludes its base because $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same fixed model and complete data, and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]). Write $\Sigma=j(\Sigma)$ and let $C_{\mathrm{corr}}\subseteq\partial U$ be its corresponding-boundary set. All causal relations and future normals below use the original $N,N'$. A tangent vector $v$ is future timelike when $g(v,v)<0$ and $g(v,N)<0$, in the convention of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. If $C_{\mathrm{corr}}\cap J^-(\Sigma)\ne\varnothing$, the following past-side construction exists.

**(a) Exposure and localization.** There is $p\in C_{\mathrm{corr}}\cap I^-(\Sigma)$ with

$$J^+(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^-(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$

Choose a strictly convex normal neighborhood $C_0\subseteq I^-(\Sigma)$ (every pair has a unique contained geodesic and each base exponential has a smooth inverse on $C_0$, as in [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) of $p$ with $C_0\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$. There is an open causally convex diamond $W$ containing $p$, with compact closure $\overline W\subseteq C_0$, and a point $q\in W\cap I^-(p)$ such that

$$J^+(q)\cap U^c\cap J^-(\Sigma)\subseteq W.$$

**(b) The whole restart surface.** For $x\in C_0$ put $\xi(x)=\exp_q^{-1}(x)$ and define the continuous local forward radial separation

$$r_q(x):=\begin{cases}\sqrt{-g_q(\xi(x),\xi(x))},&\xi(x)\text{ is future timelike},\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$

Set $K=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^-(\Sigma)$ and $r_0=\max_K r_q$. Then $r_0>0$, every maximizer lies in $W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, and $r_q>r_0$ in $W$ implies membership in $U$. The connected component $S$ of $\{x\in W:r_q(x)=r_0\}$ containing any chosen maximizer is a nonempty smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface without boundary, closed relative to $W$, and

$$S\subseteq (W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}),\qquad S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing.$$

**(c) Thin tubes and original-oriented comparison.** On the positive radial region put $X=-\nabla r_q$, a unit future timelike vector field, and let $F(s,t)$ be its local flow from $s\in S$. For any prescribed open neighborhood $O\subseteq W$ of the whole $S$ and positive continuous ceiling $b:S\to(0,\infty)$, there is a smooth positive width $\delta\le b$ with $\delta<r_0/8$ such that, on $\mathcal D_\delta=\{(s,t):s\in S,\ |t|<\delta(s)\}$, $F$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open tube $\mathcal N\subseteq O$ and $r_q(F(s,t))=r_0+t$. Write $q_0=g|_{TS}$ and $q_t=F_t^*g|_{TS}$. One has $F^*g=-dt^2+q_t$, $q_t\ge q_0/2$, and $|d\delta|_{q_0}\le1/(8\sqrt2)$. Moreover:

1. causal curves in $\mathcal N$ are graphs in $t$, with finite total $q_0$-length of their base projections, and meet $S$ at most once;
2. every causal curve inextendible in $U\cup\mathcal N$ meets the original $\Sigma$ exactly once;
3. for $y=F(s,t_y)\in\mathcal N\cap U$, the radial segment between $0$ and $t_y$, excluding its base $s$, lies in $U$. If $t_y<0$ then $s\in U$, and whenever $s\in U$ the inclusive segment lies in $U$. If a local isometry $\Theta:\mathcal N\to M'$ preserves the original time orientation and agrees on $S$ with the corresponding-set smooth extension $\Phi$, then $\Theta=\varphi$ on $\mathcal N\cap U$;
4. every smaller smooth positive width $\widetilde\delta\le\delta$ with $|d\widetilde\delta|_{q_0}\le1/(4\sqrt2)$ retains conclusions 1-3. Such a width exists inside any further prescribed open neighborhood of $S$ and below any further positive continuous ceiling, by the same construction.

No matter field, future unit normal, initial second fundamental form or complete model data is reversed. In particular the past-side construction applies to every fixed admissible model of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]], without a model time-reversal assumption. No compactness of $S$ or uniform positive lower bound for the tube width is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$$C:=\{p\in\partial U:\ p\text{ has a corresponding boundary point in }\partial\varphi(U)\}$$
be the set of boundary points of $U$ that have a corresponding point (clause
(c) of that definition). Then:

**(a)** $C$ is open in $\partial U$: there is an open set $G\subseteq M$ with
$C=G\cap\partial U$.

**(b)** There is an open set $\Omega\subseteq M$ with $U\cup C\subseteq\Omega$
and a smooth map $\Phi:\Omega\to M'$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\varphi$ and
whose value at $p\in C$ is the unique corresponding boundary point of $p$;
moreover, for every $p\in C$ there is an open neighbourhood
$W_p\subseteq\Omega$ of $p$ and a smooth **local diffeomorphism**
$$\widehat\varphi_p:W_p\to M',\qquad \widehat\varphi_p(q)=\exp_{\varphi(a_p)}\bigl(d\varphi_{a_p}(\exp_{a_p}^{-1}q)\bigr)$$
built from a common interior base point $a_p\in U$, chosen in $I^-(p)$ when $p$ is to the future of the initial surface and in $I^+(p)$ when $p$ is to its past, and the
exponential maps, such that $\widehat\varphi_p=\varphi$ on $W_p\cap U$ and
$\Phi=\widehat\varphi_p$ on $W_p\cap(U\cup C)$. No isometry property of
$\widehat\varphi_p$ on the part of $W_p$ outside $\overline U$ is claimed.

**(c)** At every point $q\in U\cup C$ the map $\Phi$ preserves the metric, the
matter fields and the metric-selected connection:

1. $g'_{\Phi(q)}(d\Phi_qv,d\Phi_qw)=g_q(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_qM$, so
   $\Phi^*(g')=g$ on $U\cup C$;
2. $(\Phi^*\psi'^i)_q=\psi^i_q$ for every listed matter field $i$;
3. for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ defined on a neighbourhood of $q$ and
   every $q\in U\cup C$,
   $$\nabla'_{d\Phi\,X}d\Phi\,Y=d\Phi\bigl(\nabla_XY\bigr)\quad\text{at }\Phi(q),$$
   equivalently the pullback connection $\Phi^*\nabla'$ equals $\nabla$ at
   $q$, where both sides are read through the invertible differential
   $d\Phi_q$.

**(d)** Every geodesic segment of $(M,g)$ whose image is contained in $U\cup C$
is mapped by $\Phi$ to a geodesic segment of $(M',g')$; a null geodesic
segment is mapped to a null geodesic segment.

**(e)** Let $S\subseteq U\cup C$ be an embedded submanifold of $M$. Then
$\Phi|_S$ is an injective immersion, hence an embedding onto its image, and it
carries the induced metric of $S$, its second fundamental form with respect to
any unit normal field, and the matter fields together with their covariant derivatives of every finite order along $S$ to the corresponding objects of $\Phi(S)$ in
$M'$. In particular $(S,\bar g_S,k_S,\psi|_S)$ and
$(\Phi(S),\bar g_{\Phi(S)},k_{\Phi(S)},\psi'|_{\Phi(S)})$ are identified by
$\Phi|_S$ whenever $S$ is spacelike.

**Data.** Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $K$. The normal convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Specify one fixed covariant matter model, consisting of a finite list of smooth tensor fields $\psi$, fixed equations $\mathcal E(g,\psi)=0$ and a fixed stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\psi)$, with pullback by local diffeomorphisms commuting with the equations and stress. Fix its complete smooth Cauchy data $d$: these determine all independent matter initial variables, not only the normal stress projections. Initial tensors with normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb R\nu\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $g_0(a\nu+X,b\nu+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. In a development, identify $a\nu+X$ with $an+dj(X)$.

An admissible fixed coupled model is one satisfying the complete initialization, hyperbolic reduction, recovery and comparison hypotheses of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]], or a specified independent local existence and uniqueness reduction such as the dust branch below. The same fixed model, complete data and admissibility conditions are used in every comparison and at every restart. Admissibility includes the applicability of its supplied complete-data local existence and geometric uniqueness theorem to the data realized on each spacelike restart surface of the compared solutions. This must be checked for the actual model and surface; it is not inferred from stress conservation. This class includes the following four concrete branches; they do not exhaust it.

1. **Vacuum:** no matter fields, $\mathcal T=0$, and empty matter data.
2. **Scalar field:** fix one smooth potential $V$ and one normalization $K_\phi>0$. The field is $\varphi$, its equation is $\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$, its stress is the expression in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] clause (c), and its complete data are $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ with $\pi_0=n(\varphi)|_\Sigma$. The fixed potential has no sign restriction ([[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]).
3. **Strict barotropic fluid:** fix a smooth EOS $P:J\to\mathbb R$ on an open interval with $\epsilon+P(\epsilon)>0$ and $0<P'(\epsilon)<1$. The fields are $\epsilon\in J$ and future unit velocity $u$, the stress is $(\epsilon+P(\epsilon))u^\flat\otimes u^\flat+P(\epsilon)g$, and the equations are the continuity and Euler equations of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] clause (c), with this fixed EOS. Complete data are $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$, where $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, equivalently the bundle velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(\nu+v_0)$. No small-tilt restriction is imposed ([[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]]).
4. **Geodesic nonnegative dust:** the fields are an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon\ge0$ and a smooth future unit timelike field $u$, including on $\{\varepsilon=0\}$. Set $\mathcal T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$ and require both $\nabla_u u=0$ and $u(\varepsilon)+\varepsilon\nabla_a u^a=0$ everywhere. Complete data are $(\varepsilon_0,U_0)$, with $\varepsilon_0\ge0$ and prescribed smooth future unit bundle velocity $U_0$, equivalently arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt. On positive-density regions this is [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]] with its density parameter equal to $\varepsilon$. Through empty regions the geodesic velocity is separately prescribed and matched; conservation of stress alone is not substituted for this full system. For a fixed $c>0$, the mass-normalized theorem [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] applies with $\rho_0=\varepsilon_0/c^2$ and reconstructs $\varepsilon=c^2\rho$.

Require the constraints for the initial stress $T_0$ computed from this complete data on $\mathcal V$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(\nu,\nu),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(\nu,\cdot).$$
These use the convention of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]. Equality of data includes equality of the model, constants, potential or EOS, and every component of $d$.

The local Cauchy-development and uniqueness suppliers for vacuum, scalar and strict fluid are the fixed-model theorem [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] and the two concrete branch theorems above. Its harmonic route requires the same fixed extraction/reconstruction rules and smooth symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family for every compared physical solution, a positive time matrix on an admissible open state set, complete compatible initialization from $(h,K,d)$, propagation of auxiliary compatibility with recovery of the full matter equations on the reduced solution, and stress conservation on that reduced solution before Einstein recovery. These are the three explicit hypotheses of that theorem; conservation alone does not supply a Cauchy evolution law. Dust uses its independent common-flow/parallel-frame initialization, hyperbolic reduction, subsidiary recovery and uniqueness of [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]], rather than being asserted to satisfy the harmonic metric-first-derivative matter contract. Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are carried wherever these local theorems are invoked. Every additional fixed coupled model must supply the same complete-data local existence, admissibility, recovery and uniqueness obligations before it is used. This definition makes no local or global existence assertion.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. the smooth tensor fields $\psi$ of the fixed model over $M$;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $d$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$: the isometry carries the future cone of $N$ onto that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, with the natural pullback action on every listed tensor type (and the inverse differential on contravariant slots). Equality includes every listed field, including the prescribed dust velocity at zero density.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,d)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one scalar model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], with its fixed smooth potential and normalization. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$ and complete scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$. Suppose the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold for the scalar stress computed from these data, with $\pi_0$ the prescribed future-normal derivative. Then there is a smooth local Einstein-scalar development
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad \Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,$$
with induced geometric data $(h,K_2)$, $\varphi|_\Sigma=\varphi_0$ and $n(\varphi)|_\Sigma=\pi_0$. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width. The initial surface is interior to its intrinsic domain of dependence; restricting to the interior Cauchy neighborhood gives a globally hyperbolic development. Every two developments of this same fixed model and complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\varphi$. No potential positivity, mass sign, global existence or uniform noncompact slab is asserted ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$, density $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and tangent field $v_0$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$. These specify the future unit initial velocity
$$U_0=W_0(N+v_0),\qquad W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$$
in $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for
$$T_0=(\epsilon_0+p(\epsilon_0))U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}+p(\epsilon_0)g_0.$$
Then a smooth time-oriented local development has metric $g$, density $\epsilon$ and future unit fluid velocity $u$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\left[(\epsilon+p)u_au_b+pg_{ab}\right],\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+\Pi^{ba}\partial_ap=0.$$
Here $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$. Initial geometric data are $(h,K_2)$ and initial matter data are $(\epsilon_0,U_0)$ under $N\mapsto n$, $X\mapsto i_*X$. Arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt is allowed. The initial surface lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence; its interior Cauchy neighborhood is globally hyperbolic. Any two developments of this same EOS and complete data agree near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing future isometry matching density and velocity. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; shocks, vacuum boundaries and vanishing sound speed are outside this strict interior-fluid statement ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix constants $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and a smooth mass-normalized density $\rho_0\ge0$. Specify initial velocity as a smooth section $U_0$ of $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with the bundle metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, satisfying $g_0(U_0,U_0)=-1$ and positive $N$ coefficient. Thus the velocity need not be normal and does not presuppose a spacetime development. Put $\varepsilon_0=\rho_0c^2$ and require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for $T_0=\varepsilon_0U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}$. On $\{\rho_0>0\}$ this is exactly the dust supplier with density parameter $\varepsilon_0$, rather than $\rho_0$ ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); zero regions have independently prescribed velocity.

Then there is a smooth local development: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian metric $g$, density $\rho\ge0$ and future unit timelike field $u$ near an embedded copy of $\Sigma$, solving
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\rho c^2u_au_b,\qquad \nabla_uu=0,\qquad u(\rho)+\rho\nabla\!\cdot u=0.$$
The induced geometric and matter data are $(h,K,\rho_0,U_0)$, with $\mathcal V$ identified by $aN+X\mapsto an+i_*X$ using the future unit normal $n$. The initial surface lies in the interior of its domain of dependence; restriction to its Cauchy neighborhood gives a local Cauchy development. Every two such developments agree near $\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\rho,u$. No division by density is used, so smooth empty regions are admitted. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; no uniform noncompact slab or continuation past flow crossings is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the locally absolutely continuous causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, and let $B_R\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be the open ball of radius $R>0$ centered at $0$, with Euclidean norm $|\cdot|$. Suppose $(s,\sigma):U\to I\times B_R$ is a diffeomorphism of an open set $U\subseteq M$, satisfying:

**(C1)** $\partial_s$ is future timelike and every $s$-level is spacelike;

**(C2)** there is $K\ge1$ such that $|d\sigma(v)|\le Kds(v)$ for every nonzero future causal vector $v$ based in $U$.

Write $S=s^{-1}(0)$, and compute the domains of dependence intrinsically in $U$:
$$D^+_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D^-_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\}.$$
Here inextendibility means absence of an endpoint limit in the specified open submanifold, and Cauchy intersection means exactly one parameter visit ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). Then:

**(a)** $D^+_U(S)\subseteq\{s\ge0\}$ and $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$.

**(b)** The corrected open collar
$$Q=\{q\in U:|\sigma(q)|+K|s(q)|<R\}$$
is a neighborhood of the entire slice $S$ in $U$ and is contained in $D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)$; more precisely $Q\cap\{s>0\}\subseteq D^+_U(S)$ and $Q\cap\{s<0\}\subseteq D^-_U(S)$.

**(c)** The open set $W=\operatorname{int}_U(D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S))$ contains $Q$, and $S$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(W,g|_W,N|_W)$. Consequently $W$ is globally hyperbolic by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(d) Generic spacelike and noncompact scope.** For every smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subseteq M$ without boundary there exist an open neighborhood $U_\Sigma$ of $\Sigma$, a smooth positive function $\delta:\Sigma\to(0,\infty)$, and a diffeomorphism
$$F:\Omega\to U_\Sigma,\qquad\Omega=\{(s,x)\in\mathbb R\times\Sigma:|s|<\delta(x)\},\qquad F(0,x)=x,$$
such that $s$ is temporal and $F_*\partial_s$ is future timelike. The intrinsic set $W_\Sigma=\operatorname{int}_{U_\Sigma}(D^+_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma)\cup D^-_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma))$ is an open neighborhood in which $\Sigma$ is Cauchy, hence is globally hyperbolic. Neither compactness nor global acausality of $\Sigma$ in $M$ is assumed. No positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause
(a), with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$. Let
$\varphi:M\to M'$ be a smooth map with $\varphi^*(g')=g$, with
$g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$, with
$\varphi\circ j=j'$ and $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$ (so $\varphi$ is a future isometric immersion fixing the complete data and matching every matter field).
Then:

**(a)** $d\varphi_p:T_pM\to T_{\varphi(p)}M'$ is an isomorphism for every
$p\in M$;

**(b)** $\varphi$ is injective, hence a diffeomorphism onto the open subset
$\varphi(M)\subseteq M'$ and therefore a development embedding in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c);

**(c)** if $M$ is connected and $\psi_1,\psi_2:M\to M'$ are two such
data-fixing isometric immersions, then $\psi_1=\psi_2$; in particular every
data-fixing self-isometry of a connected development is the identity of $M$.

Throughout, for a smooth map $\psi:N\to N'$ between smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds write $\psi^*(g')=g$ when $g_p(v,w)=g'_{\psi(p)}(d\psi_pv,d\psi_pw)$
for all $p\in N$ and $v,w\in T_pN$; such a map is an **isometric immersion**
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). Let $\nabla,\nabla'$ be
the metric-selected connections ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let geodesics
and exponential maps be those of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]].

**(a) Rigidity.** Let $N$ be connected and let
$\psi_1,\psi_2:N\to N'$ be isometric immersions with
$\psi_1(p)=\psi_2(p)$ and $d\psi_1(p)=d\psi_2(p)$ for some $p\in N$. Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$, that is, $\psi_1(q)=\psi_2(q)$ and $d\psi_1(q)=d\psi_2(q)$
for every $q\in N$.

**(b) Data-fixing embeddings have equal differentials on the initial surface.**
Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$, $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ and $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ be
as in [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a),
and let $\psi_1,\psi_2:U\to M'$ be development embeddings in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c). Then
$d\psi_1=d\psi_2$ at every point of $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$.

**(c) Agreement on overlaps.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the supplied
causal-convexity and Cauchy-side arguments in this clause. Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$
be developments of the same data, and let $(U_1,\psi_1)$ and $(U_2,\psi_2)$ be
common subdevelopments in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$ on $U_1\cap U_2$.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data
([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]), $(U,\varphi)$ a common
subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]
clause (a)), $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ be an exposed
boundary point in the sense of [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]:
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$
Fix a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $p$
([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) with $C\subseteq I^+(\Sigma)$ and
$C\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, where $C_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the
corresponding set of [[lem-gr-corresponding-set-smooth-extension]] (possible
because that set is open in $\partial U$ and $I^+(\Sigma)$ is open). Let
$p_1\ll p\ll p_2$ be points of $C$ such that $W:=I^+(p_1)\cap I^-(p_2)$
satisfies $\overline W\subseteq C$ (possible: strong causality at $p$ supplies
a neighbourhood $V_2\subseteq C$ of $p$ such that every causal curve with
both endpoints in $V_2$ is contained in $C$, and then
$\overline W\subseteq J^+(p_1)\cap J^-(p_2)\subseteq C$ for $p_1,p_2\in V_2$
by the same argument). Then $W$ is open, causally convex, $p\in W$, and
$\overline W$ is compact. Let $q\in W\cap I^+(p)$ be a point with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W,$$
chosen so close to $p$ along a future timelike curve that also $q\in W$
([[lem-gr-exposed-boundary-point]]). Let $\tau_q$ be the time separation from
$q$ ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) and put
$$K:=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma),\qquad \tau_0:=\max\{\tau_q(r):r\in K\}.$$
Let $W^\circ:=W\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and let $S$ be the connected component of
the closed-in-$W^\circ$ set $\{x\in W^\circ:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ that contains
a maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$. Then:

**(a)** $\tau_0>0$; every maximizer of $\tau_q$ over $K$ lies in
$W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$; every $x\in W$ with
$\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ lies in $U$; every $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with
$\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$ lies in $\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(b)** $S$ is a nonempty smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface of $M$
without boundary, subsets $S\subseteq(W\cap U)\cup(W\cap\partial U\cap
C_{\mathrm{corr}})$ and $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$; moreover
$S\subseteq\{x:\tau_q(x)=\tau_0\}$ and every point of $S\cap U^c$ lies in
$\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$.

**(c)** There is a smooth positive function $\delta:S\to(0,\infty)$ with the
following properties. Define $X:=\nabla\tau_q/g(\nabla\tau_q,\nabla\tau_q)$
(so that $d\tau_q(X)=1$) on $\{\tau_q>0\}\cap W$, let $\phi_t$ be its local
flow, and put
$$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to M,\qquad F(s,t):=\phi_t(s),\qquad N:=F\bigl(S\times(-\delta,\delta)\bigr).$$
Then $F$ is well defined and smooth, $N\subseteq W$ is open,
$F:S\times(-\delta,\delta)\to N$ is a diffeomorphism,
$\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$, and:

1. every causal curve in $N$ is, in the coordinates $(s,t)$, of the form
   $t\mapsto F(s(t),t)$ with $s(t)$ of finite length in the induced metric
   of $S$, and it meets $S$ in at most one parameter value;
2. every causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$ meets
   $U$, and consequently meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value; in
   particular no causal curve in $U\cup N$ that is inextendible in $U\cup N$
   and whose image is disjoint from $U$ exists;
3. for every $y\in N\cap U$ there is a unique $s\in S$ with $y=F(s,t_y)$, and the **punctured radial segment**
$$\{F(s,u):u\text{ between }0\text{ and }t_y,\ u\ne0\}$$
is contained in $U$. The base belongs to $U\cup C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, and the full segment including the base is contained in $U$ whenever $s\in U$. In particular, if $t_y<0$ then also $s\in U$. If $\Theta:N\to M'$ is a time-orientation-preserving local isometry with $\Theta|_S=\Phi|_S$, where $\Phi$ is the smooth extension of the common-subdevelopment map $\varphi$, then $\Theta=\varphi$ on $N\cap U$;
4. the tube can be chosen inside any prescribed open neighbourhood $O\subseteq W$ of the whole $S$, and below any prescribed positive continuous width ceiling on $S$. More quantitatively, write $q_0=g|_{TS}$ and $q_t=F_t^*g|_{TS}$. The construction gives $0<\delta<\tau_0/8$, $q_t\ge\tfrac12q_0$ for $|t|<\delta(s)$ and $|d\delta|_{q_0}\le1/(8\sqrt2)$. Every smooth positive smaller width $\widetilde\delta\le\delta$ satisfying $|d\widetilde\delta|_{q_0}\le1/(4\sqrt2)$ retains conclusions 1-3.

No compactness of $S$ or positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is assumed. The radial segment in clause 3 excludes its base because $S\cap\partial U\ne\varnothing$.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same fixed model and complete data, and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]]). Write $\Sigma=j(\Sigma)$ and let $C_{\mathrm{corr}}\subseteq\partial U$ be its corresponding-boundary set. All causal relations and future normals below use the original $N,N'$. A tangent vector $v$ is future timelike when $g(v,v)<0$ and $g(v,N)<0$, in the convention of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. If $C_{\mathrm{corr}}\cap J^-(\Sigma)\ne\varnothing$, the following past-side construction exists.

**(a) Exposure and localization.** There is $p\in C_{\mathrm{corr}}\cap I^-(\Sigma)$ with

$$J^+(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^-(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$

Choose a strictly convex normal neighborhood $C_0\subseteq I^-(\Sigma)$ (every pair has a unique contained geodesic and each base exponential has a smooth inverse on $C_0$, as in [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]) of $p$ with $C_0\cap\partial U\subseteq C_{\mathrm{corr}}$. There is an open causally convex diamond $W$ containing $p$, with compact closure $\overline W\subseteq C_0$, and a point $q\in W\cap I^-(p)$ such that

$$J^+(q)\cap U^c\cap J^-(\Sigma)\subseteq W.$$

**(b) The whole restart surface.** For $x\in C_0$ put $\xi(x)=\exp_q^{-1}(x)$ and define the continuous local forward radial separation

$$r_q(x):=\begin{cases}\sqrt{-g_q(\xi(x),\xi(x))},&\xi(x)\text{ is future timelike},\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$

Set $K=\overline W\cap U^c\cap J^-(\Sigma)$ and $r_0=\max_K r_q$. Then $r_0>0$, every maximizer lies in $W\cap\partial U\cap C_{\mathrm{corr}}$, and $r_q>r_0$ in $W$ implies membership in $U$.
