citations.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix the data of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$,
one fixed admissible covariant matter model with its complete smooth Cauchy
data $d$, and constants $\Lambda,\kappa$. The model and its complete data,
including all required initial derivatives and prescribed fields on empty
regions, are fixed throughout. Assume the supplied complete-data local
existence and geometric uniqueness hypotheses apply on every spacelike
restart surface occurring in comparisons, as required by that definition.
Assume that at least one development of these data exists.
Write $Z_0:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ and let $j_0:\Sigma\to Z_0$,
$j_0(x):=(x,0)$.

**(a) The set-sized family.** Let $\mathcal X$ be the collection of all
tuples $(U,g,N,\psi)$ such that $U\subseteq Z_0$ is an open neighbourhood of
$j_0(\Sigma)$ in $Z_0$, $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $U$, $N$ a time
orientation and $\psi$ matter fields of the sector on $U$, and
$(U,g,N,j_0,\psi)$ is a development of the data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a). Then
$\mathcal X$ is a set, and it is nonempty provided at least one development
of the data exists.

**(b) Identifications.** For $\alpha=(U_\alpha,g_\alpha,N_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$
and $\beta\in\mathcal X$ let $(U_{\alpha\beta},\varphi_{\alpha\beta})$ be
their maximal common development, regarded as a subset of $U_\alpha$
([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]], [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]];
in the convention of the definition it is realised inside the first member).
Let $Z:=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}U_\alpha$ and let $\sim$ be the
equivalence relation on $Z$ **generated** by the relations
$x\sim\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(x)$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal X$ and
$x\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ (a finite chain of such steps, in either order).
Then the classes of two points $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$ coincide if and
only if $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)$.

**(c) The quotient.** Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi$. Then
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset
$Q_\alpha:=\pi(U_\alpha)$, the family $\{Q_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}$
covers $Q$, and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(d) Structure.** $Q$ is a Hausdorff, second countable smooth four-manifold and carries a
unique smooth atlas (unique in the sense of maximal atlases compatible with
the charts below) making all maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms onto open
subsets, together with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, a time orientation
$\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ such that every $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ is an
isometry onto its image preserving time orientation and matter fields, and
such that $\bar j:=\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ (independent of $\alpha$) is a
common embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data $(h,K,d)$. The field
equations hold on $Q$, and every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in
$Q$ meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value. Consequently
$(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ is a development of the data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a).
The representative $\bar N$ is chosen to determine the common future cones;
it need not equal the pushforward of each representative $N_\alpha$.

**(e) Universality.** Every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data
admits a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ induced by the chart $\psi_p$ on $T_pM$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
geodesics, their maximal domains $I_{q,v}$ and the exponential maps
$\exp_q$ be those of [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Fix
$p\in M$. Write $\pi:TM\to M$ for the bundle projection.

**(a) Smoothness of the joint map.** The set
$$\mathcal D:=\{(q,v)\in TM:\ 1\in I_{q,v}\}\subseteq TM$$
is open in $TM$, and the **joint exponential map**
$$\Phi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M\times M,\qquad \Phi(q,v):=(q,\exp_q v),$$
is smooth.

**(b) Differential at $(p,0)$.** The differential $d\Phi_{(p,0)}$ is an
isomorphism. Explicitly, fix a smooth chart $(U,x)$ around $p$; it induces
the chart $(TU,Tx)$ of $TM$ and the product chart $(U\times U,x\times x)$ of
$M\times M$, and under the induced identifications
$T_{(p,0)}(TM)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ and
$T_{(p,p)}(M\times M)\cong T_pM\oplus T_pM$ one has
$$d\Phi_{(p,0)}(u,w)=(u,\ u+w)\qquad\text{for all }u,w\in T_pM .$$

**(c) Diffeomorphism and two-point inverse.** There are open neighborhoods
$V\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $(p,0)$ and $W\subseteq M\times M$ of $(p,p)$ such
that $\Phi|_V:V\to W$ is a diffeomorphism. Moreover $V$ can be chosen
product-like: there are a chart $(U,x)$ around $p$ with $x(p)=0$, a radius
$r>0$ and a velocity radius $\rho>0$ such that, writing $B_s:=\{y\in\mathbb
R^4:|y|_{\mathrm e}<s\}$,
$$V=\bigl\{(q,v):\ q\in x^{-1}(B_r),\ \text{the coordinate components of }v\text{ in }(TU,Tx)\text{ lie in }B_\rho\bigr\},$$
and there is $s\in(0,r)$ with $x^{-1}(\overline{B_s})\times x^{-1}(\overline{B_s})\subseteq W$.
Consequently the velocity map
$$v:W\longrightarrow TM,\qquad (q,r)\longmapsto v(q,r):=\text{the vector with }(q,v(q,r))\in V,\ \Phi(q,v(q,r))=(q,r),$$
is well defined and smooth, and $\exp_q\bigl(v(q,r)\bigr)=r$ for all
$(q,r)\in W$.

**(d) Lipschitz bound for the two-point inverse.** On every pair
$x^{-1}(B_s)\times x^{-1}(B_s)\subseteq W$ as in (c) there is a constant
$\Lambda\ge 0$ such that, for all $q,r\in x^{-1}(B_s)$,
$$|v(q,r)|_x\le\Lambda\,\bigl|x(q)-x(r)\bigr|_{\mathrm e},$$
where $|v|_x$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate components of
$v$ and $v(q,q)=0$. In particular $|v(q,r)|_x\le 2\Lambda s$ on this pair.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Recall that a natural number is a von Neumann natural
([[def-natural-numbers]]): $0 = \varnothing$ and $\sigma(n) = n \cup \{n\}$, so
that

$$n = \{\, m \in \mathbb{N} : m < n \,\} = \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$$

is itself the set of its predecessors. Here $<$ is the order of
[[def-nat-order]], which is defined additively, so the displayed identity is a
theorem and not a convention: it is [[lem-nat-order-is-membership]], proved
immediately above. Let $A$ be a set, and let $\approx$ be equinumerosity
([[def-equinumerous]]).

- $A$ is **finite** if $A \approx n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
- $A$ is **countably infinite** if $A \approx \mathbb{N}$.
- $A$ is **at most countable** if it is finite or countably infinite.
- $A$ is **uncountable** if it is not at most countable.

**Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice** ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(A_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a family of at most countable sets
([[def-countable]]) indexed by $\mathbb{N}$. Then

$$U = \bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} A_n$$

is at most countable.

**The role of $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.** It is spent at exactly one step, step 3.1 below, where a surjection $\mathbb N\to A_n$ is selected simultaneously for each nonempty $A_n$. The individual countability hypotheses assert that these sets of surjections are nonempty; they specify no simultaneous selection.

Write $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ for the image of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{R}$
under the canonical embedding $q \mapsto \hat q$ ([[lem-rat-embeds-dense]]), the
set usually written $\mathbb{Q}$ once the identification is made, and put
$X := \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ for the irrationals. Then:

1. $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$, that is,
   $\overline{\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}} = \mathbb{R}$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]);
2. $X$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$;
3. every nonempty open subset of $\mathbb{R}$ is uncountable
   ([[def-countable]]).

Claim 2 is not a symmetry of claim 1: the rationals are dense because they are
*constructed* to approximate, whereas the irrationals are dense because there are
too many points in any interval for a countable set to exhaust it, which is why
claim 3 is proved alongside and used for it.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T})$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]).

A family $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ is a **basis for $\mathcal{T}$** if
every open set is a union of members of $\mathcal{B}$: for every
$U \in \mathcal{T}$ there is $\mathcal{B}_U \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ with
$U = \bigcup \mathcal{B}_U$. Equivalently, and this is the form used in proofs,

$$\text{for every } U \in \mathcal{T} \text{ and every } x \in U \text{ there is } B \in \mathcal{B} \text{ with } x \in B \subseteq U .$$

*The two forms say the same thing.* If every open $U$ is such a union and
$x \in U$, then $x$ lies in one of the sets united, which is a member of
$\mathcal{B}$ inside $U$. Conversely, if the displayed condition holds then
$U = \bigcup \{\, B \in \mathcal{B} : B \subseteq U \,\}$, since each such $B$ is
contained in $U$ and each $x \in U$ lies in one of them. Note that
$\bigcup \varnothing = \varnothing$, so the empty open set is covered by the empty
subfamily and needs no member of $\mathcal{B}$. The members of a basis are called
**basic open sets**.

**The topology generated by a family.** Let $\mathcal{S} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(X)$
be *any* family of subsets of $X$. Then

$$\langle \mathcal{S} \rangle := \bigcap \{\, \mathcal{T}' : \mathcal{T}' \text{ is a topology on } X \text{ with } \mathcal{S} \subseteq \mathcal{T}' \,\}$$

is a topology on $X$, it contains $\mathcal{S}$, and it is contained in every
topology on $X$ that contains $\mathcal{S}$. It is called the **topology
generated by $\mathcal{S}$**, and $\mathcal{S}$ is a **subbasis** for a topology
$\mathcal{T}$ when $\mathcal{T} = \langle \mathcal{S} \rangle$.

*This is well posed, and the obligation is discharged here.* The collection being
intersected is nonempty, because $\mathcal{P}(X)$ is a topology on $X$ containing
$\mathcal{S}$; so the intersection is an intersection of a nonempty family of
subsets of $\mathcal{P}(X)$ and is a set. It is a topology: $\varnothing$ and $X$
lie in every topology on $X$, hence in the intersection, which is (T1); if
$\mathcal{S}' \subseteq \langle \mathcal{S} \rangle$ then $\mathcal{S}'$ is a
subfamily of each $\mathcal{T}'$ in the collection, so $\bigcup \mathcal{S}'$ lies
in each $\mathcal{T}'$ and hence in the intersection, which is (T2); and the same
argument with $U \cap V$ gives (T3). It contains $\mathcal{S}$ because every
$\mathcal{T}'$ in the collection does, and it is contained in each such
$\mathcal{T}'$ because an intersection is contained in each of its members. So
$\langle \mathcal{S} \rangle$ is the coarsest topology on $X$ containing
$\mathcal{S}$ ([[def-topological-space]]), and in particular it is uniquely
determined by $\mathcal{S}$.

**Neither notion is intrinsic to the family alone.** "$\mathcal{B}$ is a basis
for $\mathcal{T}$" and "$\mathcal{S}$ is a subbasis for $\mathcal{T}$" are
relations between a family and a topology, not properties of the family. The
question of which families are a basis *for some* topology, and how the topology
generated by a subbasis is computed from it, is settled by the next item.

derivations.claim: (Countability and openness.) Use [L3] to choose the tangent bases. The family $\mathcal B$ is the image of a subset of the countable indexing set $D\times\mathbb Q^4\times\mathbb Q_{>0}$ and hence countable. Each member is open by the defining diffeomorphism condition. No arbitrary small exponential domain is fixed at a dense center.

(The basis criterion.) Let $p\in O\subseteq Q$ with $O$ open. Choose a member containing $p$ and the product neighborhood of $(p,p)$ supplied by [L2]. Its first factor is an open neighborhood $V$ of $p$ in $Q$. Choose $d\in D\cap V$ by density. The inverse velocity $v(d,p)$ lies in $H_d$, where $\exp_d$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of this member. Thus $H_d\cap\exp_d^{-1}(O)$ is an open neighborhood of $v(d,p)$ in $T_dQ$. In the chosen basis at $d$, select a rational translated ball $B_d(a,r)$ containing $v(d,p)$ and contained in this neighborhood by [L3]. By [L1]-[L2], the quotient exponential on this ball agrees with the member exponential and restricts to a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $Q$, so its image belongs to $\mathcal B$ and satisfies $p\in\exp_d(B_d(a,r))\subseteq O$.

(Conclusion.) Steps 1.1 and 2.1 show that $\mathcal B$ is a countable family of open sets satisfying the basis criterion. Therefore it is a countable basis and $Q$ is second countable ([[def-second-countable-space]]).

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix the data of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$,
one fixed admissible covariant matter model with its complete smooth Cauchy
data $d$, and constants $\Lambda,\kappa$. The model and its complete data,
including all required initial derivatives and prescribed fields on empty
regions, are fixed throughout. Assume the supplied complete-data local
existence and geometric uniqueness hypotheses apply on every spacelike
restart surface occurring in comparisons, as required by that definition.
Assume that at least one development of these data exists.
Write $Z_0:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ and let $j_0:\Sigma\to Z_0$,
$j_0(x):=(x,0)$.

**(a) The set-sized family.** Let $\mathcal X$ be the collection of all
tuples $(U,g,N,\psi)$ such that $U\subseteq Z_0$ is an open neighbourhood of
$j_0(\Sigma)$ in $Z_0$, $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $U$, $N$ a time
orientation and $\psi$ matter fields of the sector on $U$, and
$(U,g,N,j_0,\psi)$ is a development of the data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a). Then
$\mathcal X$ is a set, and it is nonempty provided at least one development
of the data exists.

**(b) Identifications.** For $\alpha=(U_\alpha,g_\alpha,N_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)$
and $\beta\in\mathcal X$ let $(U_{\alpha\beta},\varphi_{\alpha\beta})$ be
their maximal common development, regarded as a subset of $U_\alpha$
([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]], [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]];
in the convention of the definition it is realised inside the first member).
Let $Z:=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}U_\alpha$ and let $\sim$ be the
equivalence relation on $Z$ **generated** by the relations
$x\sim\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(x)$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal X$ and
$x\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ (a finite chain of such steps, in either order).
Then the classes of two points $p\in U_\alpha$, $q\in U_\beta$ coincide if and
only if $p\in U_{\alpha\beta}$ and $q=\varphi_{\alpha\beta}(p)$.

**(c) The quotient.** Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi$. Then
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset
$Q_\alpha:=\pi(U_\alpha)$, the family $\{Q_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal X}$
covers $Q$, and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(d) Structure.** $Q$ is a Hausdorff, second countable smooth four-manifold and carries a
unique smooth atlas (unique in the sense of maximal atlases compatible with
the charts below) making all maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms onto open
subsets, together with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, a time orientation
$\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ such that every $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ is an
isometry onto its image preserving time orientation and matter fields, and
such that $\bar j:=\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ (independent of $\alpha$) is a
common embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data $(h,K,d)$. The field
equations hold on $Q$, and every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in
$Q$ meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value. Consequently
$(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ is a development of the data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a).
The representative $\bar N$ is chosen to determine the common future cones;
it need not equal the pushforward of each representative $N_\alpha$.

**(e) Universality.** Every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data
admits a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ and the
family of member maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as
in [[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d), so that $Q$ is a
Hausdorff locally Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian
metric $\bar g$, the sets $Q_\alpha$ are open and cover $Q$, and
$\bar j(\Sigma)\subseteq Q$ is the embedded initial surface. Then there is a
countable subset $D\subseteq Q$ with:

**(a)** $D\cap\bar j(\Sigma)$ is dense in $\bar j(\Sigma)$; and

**(b)** $D$ is dense in $Q$.

Moreover $D$ can be chosen of the following explicit form: with
$D_0:=S_0$ a countable dense subset of $\bar j(\Sigma)$, and having chosen
once at its first occurrence for every $x\in D_n$ a basis $(e_1(x),\dots,e_4(x))$ of $T_xQ$ and defined
$$V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}:=\Bigl\{\sum_{i=1}^4q_ie_i(x):\ q_i\in\mathbb Q\Bigr\},$$
one sets
$$D_{n+1}:=D_n\cup\bigl\{\exp_x(v):\ x\in D_n,\ v\in V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}\text{ timelike, with }\exp_x(v)\text{ defined}\bigr\},\qquad D:=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}D_n.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ and the member maps
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as in
[[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d): $Q$ is a Hausdorff locally
Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, the
open sets $Q_\alpha$ cover $Q$, and each $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$
is a diffeomorphism onto $Q_\alpha$. Let $D\subseteq Q$ be a countable dense
subset, as supplied by [[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]]. When
$Q$ and $D$ are obtained from these development suppliers, retain their
Countable Choice and Dependent Choice hypotheses ([[def-dependent-choice]]).
The basis construction conditional on the supplied $Q,D$ uses Countable
Choice only. Choose one
basis at each $d\in D$. In these coordinates let
$B_d(a,r)\subseteq T_dQ$ be the Euclidean open ball centered at
$a\in\mathbb Q^4$ with radius $r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$, and let
$\mathcal E_d$ be the maximal exponential domain. Then
$$\mathcal B:=\{\exp_d(B_d(a,r)):d\in D, a\in\mathbb Q^4, r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}, B_d(a,r)\subseteq\mathcal E_d, \exp_d|_{B_d(a,r)}\text{ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of }Q\}$$
is a countable basis of the topology of $Q$. This exhibits an explicit basis
for the second-countability conclusion of
[[lem-gr-universal-development]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause
(a), with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$. Let
$\varphi:M\to M'$ be a smooth map with $\varphi^*(g')=g$, with
$g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$, with
$\varphi\circ j=j'$ and $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$ (so $\varphi$ is a future isometric immersion fixing the complete data and matching every matter field).
Then:

**(a)** $d\varphi_p:T_pM\to T_{\varphi(p)}M'$ is an isomorphism for every
$p\in M$;

**(b)** $\varphi$ is injective, hence a diffeomorphism onto the open subset
$\varphi(M)\subseteq M'$ and therefore a development embedding in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c);

**(c)** if $M$ is connected and $\psi_1,\psi_2:M\to M'$ are two such
data-fixing isometric immersions, then $\psi_1=\psi_2$; in particular every
data-fixing self-isometry of a connected development is the identity of $M$.

Throughout, for a smooth map $\psi:N\to N'$ between smooth Lorentzian
four-manifolds write $\psi^*(g')=g$ when $g_p(v,w)=g'_{\psi(p)}(d\psi_pv,d\psi_pw)$
for all $p\in N$ and $v,w\in T_pN$; such a map is an **isometric immersion**
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). Let $\nabla,\nabla'$ be
the metric-selected connections ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let geodesics
and exponential maps be those of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]].

**(a) Rigidity.** Let $N$ be connected and let
$\psi_1,\psi_2:N\to N'$ be isometric immersions with
$\psi_1(p)=\psi_2(p)$ and $d\psi_1(p)=d\psi_2(p)$ for some $p\in N$. Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$, that is, $\psi_1(q)=\psi_2(q)$ and $d\psi_1(q)=d\psi_2(q)$
for every $q\in N$.

**(b) Data-fixing embeddings have equal differentials on the initial surface.**
Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$, $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ and $(U,g|_U,N|_U,j,\psi|_U)$ be
as in [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a),
and let $\psi_1,\psi_2:U\to M'$ be development embeddings in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c). Then
$d\psi_1=d\psi_2$ at every point of $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)\subseteq U$.

**(c) Agreement on overlaps.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the supplied
causal-convexity and Cauchy-side arguments in this clause. Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$
be developments of the same data, and let $(U_1,\psi_1)$ and $(U_2,\psi_2)$ be
common subdevelopments in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Then
$\psi_1=\psi_2$ on $U_1\cap U_2$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

**Data.** Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, a smooth three-manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary, a smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $K$. The normal convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Specify one fixed covariant matter model, consisting of a finite list of smooth tensor fields $\psi$, fixed equations $\mathcal E(g,\psi)=0$ and a fixed stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\psi)$, with pullback by local diffeomorphisms commuting with the equations and stress. Fix its complete smooth Cauchy data $d$: these determine all independent matter initial variables, not only the normal stress projections. Initial tensors with normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb R\nu\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $g_0(a\nu+X,b\nu+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. In a development, identify $a\nu+X$ with $an+dj(X)$.

An admissible fixed coupled model is one satisfying the complete initialization, hyperbolic reduction, recovery and comparison hypotheses of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]], or a specified independent local existence and uniqueness reduction such as the dust branch below. The same fixed model, complete data and admissibility conditions are used in every comparison and at every restart. Admissibility includes the applicability of its supplied complete-data local existence and geometric uniqueness theorem to the data realized on each spacelike restart surface of the compared solutions. This must be checked for the actual model and surface; it is not inferred from stress conservation. This class includes the following four concrete branches; they do not exhaust it.

1. **Vacuum:** no matter fields, $\mathcal T=0$, and empty matter data.
2. **Scalar field:** fix one smooth potential $V$ and one normalization $K_\phi>0$. The field is $\varphi$, its equation is $\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$, its stress is the expression in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] clause (c), and its complete data are $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ with $\pi_0=n(\varphi)|_\Sigma$. The fixed potential has no sign restriction ([[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]).
3. **Strict barotropic fluid:** fix a smooth EOS $P:J\to\mathbb R$ on an open interval with $\epsilon+P(\epsilon)>0$ and $0<P'(\epsilon)<1$. The fields are $\epsilon\in J$ and future unit velocity $u$, the stress is $(\epsilon+P(\epsilon))u^\flat\otimes u^\flat+P(\epsilon)g$, and the equations are the continuity and Euler equations of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] clause (c), with this fixed EOS. Complete data are $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$, where $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, equivalently the bundle velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(\nu+v_0)$. No small-tilt restriction is imposed ([[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]]).
4. **Geodesic nonnegative dust:** the fields are an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon\ge0$ and a smooth future unit timelike field $u$, including on $\{\varepsilon=0\}$. Set $\mathcal T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$ and require both $\nabla_u u=0$ and $u(\varepsilon)+\varepsilon\nabla_a u^a=0$ everywhere. Complete data are $(\varepsilon_0,U_0)$, with $\varepsilon_0\ge0$ and prescribed smooth future unit bundle velocity $U_0$, equivalently arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt. On positive-density regions this is [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]] with its density parameter equal to $\varepsilon$. Through empty regions the geodesic velocity is separately prescribed and matched; conservation of stress alone is not substituted for this full system. For a fixed $c>0$, the mass-normalized theorem [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] applies with $\rho_0=\varepsilon_0/c^2$ and reconstructs $\varepsilon=c^2\rho$.

Require the constraints for the initial stress $T_0$ computed from this complete data on $\mathcal V$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(\nu,\nu),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(\nu,\cdot).$$
These use the convention of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]. Equality of data includes equality of the model, constants, potential or EOS, and every component of $d$.

The local Cauchy-development and uniqueness suppliers for vacuum, scalar and strict fluid are the fixed-model theorem [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] and the two concrete branch theorems above. Its harmonic route requires the same fixed extraction/reconstruction rules and smooth symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family for every compared physical solution, a positive time matrix on an admissible open state set, complete compatible initialization from $(h,K,d)$, propagation of auxiliary compatibility with recovery of the full matter equations on the reduced solution, and stress conservation on that reduced solution before Einstein recovery. These are the three explicit hypotheses of that theorem; conservation alone does not supply a Cauchy evolution law. Dust uses its independent common-flow/parallel-frame initialization, hyperbolic reduction, subsidiary recovery and uniqueness of [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]], rather than being asserted to satisfy the harmonic metric-first-derivative matter contract. Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are carried wherever these local theorems are invoked. Every additional fixed coupled model must supply the same complete-data local existence, admissibility, recovery and uniqueness obligations before it is used. This definition makes no local or global existence assertion.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. the smooth tensor fields $\psi$ of the fixed model over $M$;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $d$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$: the isometry carries the future cone of $N$ onto that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, with the natural pullback action on every listed tensor type (and the inverse differential on contravariant slots). Equality includes every listed field, including the prescribed dust velocity at zero density.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,d)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

3. **Strict barotropic fluid:** fix a smooth EOS $P:J\to\mathbb R$ on an open interval with $\epsilon+P(\epsilon)>0$ and $0<P'(\epsilon)<1$. The fields are $\epsilon\in J$ and future unit velocity $u$, the stress is $(\epsilon+P(\epsilon))u^\flat\otimes u^\flat+P(\epsilon)g$, and the equations are the continuity and Euler equations of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] clause (c), with this fixed EOS. Complete data are $(\epsilon_0,v_0)$, where $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and $h(v_0,v_0)<1$, equivalently the bundle velocity $U_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}(\nu+v_0)$. No small-tilt restriction is imposed ([[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]]).
4. **Geodesic nonnegative dust:** the fields are an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon\ge0$ and a smooth future unit timelike field $u$, including on $\{\varepsilon=0\}$. Set $\mathcal T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$ and require both $\nabla_u u=0$ and $u(\varepsilon)+\varepsilon\nabla_a u^a=0$ everywhere. Complete data are $(\varepsilon_0,U_0)$, with $\varepsilon_0\ge0$ and prescribed smooth future unit bundle velocity $U_0$, equivalently arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt. On positive-density regions this is [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]] with its density parameter equal to $\varepsilon$. Through empty regions the geodesic velocity is separately prescribed and matched; conservation of stress alone is not substituted for this full system. For a fixed $c>0$, the mass-normalized theorem [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] applies with $\rho_0=\varepsilon_0/c^2$ and reconstructs $\varepsilon=c^2\rho$.

Require the constraints for the initial stress $T_0$ computed from this complete data on $\mathcal V$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(\nu,\nu),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(\nu,\cdot).$$
These use the convention of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]. Equality of data includes equality of the model, constants, potential or EOS, and every component of $d$.

The local Cauchy-development and uniqueness suppliers for vacuum, scalar and strict fluid are the fixed-model theorem [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] and the two concrete branch theorems above. Its harmonic route requires the same fixed extraction/reconstruction rules and smooth symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family for every compared physical solution, a positive time matrix on an admissible open state set, complete compatible initialization from $(h,K,d)$, propagation of auxiliary compatibility with recovery of the full matter equations on the reduced solution, and stress conservation on that reduced solution before Einstein recovery. These are the three explicit hypotheses of that theorem; conservation alone does not supply a Cauchy evolution law. Dust uses its independent common-flow/parallel-frame initialization, hyperbolic reduction, subsidiary recovery and uniqueness of [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]], rather than being asserted to satisfy the harmonic metric-first-derivative matter contract. Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are carried wherever these local theorems are invoked. Every additional fixed coupled model must supply the same complete-data local existence, admissibility, recovery and uniqueness obligations before it is used. This definition makes no local or global existence assertion.

**(a) Development.** A **development** of this data is a tuple
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ consisting of:

1. a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$
   ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
2. a smooth embedding $j:\Sigma\to M$ whose image $j(\Sigma)$ is a spacelike
   embedded hypersurface ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (a));
3. the smooth tensor fields $\psi$ of the fixed model over $M$;
4. the equations on $M$: $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab}(g,\psi)$ with
   the Einstein tensor of $g$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]])
   and $E(g,\psi)=0$;
5. the initial condition on $j(\Sigma)$: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of
   $(M,g,N)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]
   clause (c), that is, every inextendible causal curve of
   [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] meets $j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one
   parameter value;
6. the induced data: $j^*(g)=h$, the second fundamental form of $j$ with
   respect to the future unit normal equals $K$ in the convention
   $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ of
   [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], and
   the initial data of $\psi$ on $j(\Sigma)$ transported by $j$ equal $d$.

No completeness of $(M,g)$, no inextendibility of $M$, and no claim that the
equations hold beyond $M$ are part of the definition. Whether a development is
globally hyperbolic is not part of the definition either; by clause 5 it
follows from [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(b) Data-fixing isometry.** A **data-fixing isometry** between developments
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data is a smooth
diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ such that

1. $\varphi^*(g')=g$;
2. $g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$: the isometry carries the future cone of $N$ onto that of $N'$;
3. $\varphi\circ j=j'$;
4. $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$, with the natural pullback action on every listed tensor type (and the inverse differential on contravariant slots). Equality includes every listed field, including the prescribed dust velocity at zero density.

**(c) Development embedding.** A **development embedding** of $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$
into $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ is a smooth map $\varphi:M\to M'$ that is a
diffeomorphism onto an open subset of $M'$ and satisfies clauses (b)1-4.
Development embeddings are isometric immersions by clause (b)1.

**(d) Maximality.** A development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the given data is
**maximal** when for every development $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ of the same data
there exists a development embedding $\varphi:M'\to M$. A maximal development
is also called a **maximal globally hyperbolic development** of the data.

**(e) Scope.** This is a mathematical definition of the solution class used by
the Cauchy problem. The physical reading of $(M,g,N)$ and $\psi$ and the
status of $(h,K,d)$ as initial data of a model of nature are supplied by
the framework postulates of the physics library, not here; and no existence,
uniqueness or maximality assertion is made by this definition.

derivations.claim: (Existence.) Let $Q$ be the quotient of [[lem-gr-universal-development]]. By [L1] it is Hausdorff and locally Euclidean with a smooth atlas, metric, time orientation and matter fields; by [L2] it is second countable; by [L1] its initial surface is met exactly once by every inextendible causal curve and the field equations and induced data hold. Hence by [L6] $Q$ is a development of the data.

(Maximality.) Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ be a development of the data. By [L3] there is a data-fixing development embedding $\Phi:M\to Q$. Hence every development admits a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$, which is the maximality property of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (d).

(Uniqueness.) Let $Q,Q'$ both be maximal developments of the data. By maximality of $Q'$ applied to the development $Q$, there is a data-fixing development embedding $\Phi:Q\to Q'$; by maximality of $Q$ applied to $Q'$, there is $\Phi':Q'\to Q$. The composition $\Phi'\circ\Phi:Q\to Q$ is a data-fixing isometric immersion of the development $Q$ into itself (compositions of isometric immersions preserving the data and the time orientation are again such); by [L4] it is the identity of $Q$ because $Q$ is connected by [L5]. Similarly $\Phi\circ\Phi'=\mathrm{id}_{Q'}$. Hence $\Phi$ is a data-fixing isometry with inverse $\Phi'$, and $Q,Q'$ are isometric over the data.

(Uniqueness of the isometry.) If $\Phi_1,\Phi_2:Q\to Q'$ are both data-fixing isometries, then on the connected development $Q$ the two data-fixing isometric immersions coincide by [L4]; hence the isometry is unique.

(Conclusion.) The preceding steps show that the quotient $Q$ of [[lem-gr-universal-development]] is a maximal development of the data to which every development embeds by a data-fixing development embedding, and that any two maximal developments are related by exactly one data-fixing isometry. This is the assertion.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework the
following statements.

**(i) Spacetime model.** The spacetime of a model of the framework is a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ as in
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: a smooth four-manifold $M$ without
boundary, a Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and a time orientation $N$. Its points represent
idealized physical events; the vector $N$ fixes which causal directions are
future-directed; and the causal classification of tangent vectors along any
worldline is the classification of the Lorentz vector spaces $(T_pM,g_p)$
together with the future/past convention of the time orientation. The metric
$g$ is the gravitational field of the model: it is the object that the field
law of the framework constrains, and the curvature $R^g$ of the uniquely constructed torsion-free
$g$-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ of
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] is the model's representation of
gravity. That supplier defines $R^g(X,Y)Z=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z$
and proves the connection exists; this clause adds no independent connection
field. The rules by which ideal clocks, test bodies and
light rays couple to $g$ are adopted separately as physical assumptions of the
framework.

**(ii) Classical domain.** Geometry and matter are treated as classical
continuum fields: the model describes macroscopic configurations of matter and
a classical metric, with no quantum description of either. The framework makes
no claim that a real spacetime is exactly such a manifold, that matter is
exactly a classical continuum, or that the smooth description applies to
arbitrarily small scales or arbitrarily strong fields; those are domain
limitations of the model family, not consequences of it.

**(iii) Unity of the model.** A model of the framework is specified by its
geometry $(M,g,N)$ together with its matter content and the field law adopted
for it; the geometry alone selects no matter configuration and no dynamics
(the matter assumptions are
adopted separately, in the companion postulate on matter content). Physical
parameters enter through
the unit conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]; no
numerical value of a constant is asserted here.

**(iv) Smooth-branch restriction.** The fields of a model are defined on an
open domain of $M$; the metric is $C^\infty$ on all of $M$ and $M$ has no
boundary. Configurations in which a field fails to be smooth on a nonempty open
set, in which matter is concentrated on a lower-dimensional set in a way that
produces a distributional stress-energy tensor, or in which $M$ carries a
boundary, are outside the stated smooth domain of the framework and require
mathematics not supplied by these postulates.

**(v) Status.** These are adopted assumptions. They are not derived from the
mathematics of manifolds, from any symmetry principle, or from experiment; the
equivalence principle and covariance arguments motivate but do not prove them.
Testing the framework means comparing predictions computed from a fully
specified model — geometry, matter content and field law — with observations,
and agreement is evidence about the model, not a proof of these postulates.

Adopt as the field law of the direct-equation presentation of the classical
gravitational framework, for models satisfying
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], the following statement.

**(i) The equation.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab}$ be the Einstein tensor of that
connection ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$T$ be the model's stress-energy tensor field on its matter domain
$U\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) and let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant parameter with dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $G_N>0$, $c>0$ the constants of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Adopt

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U$$

as the field law of the model. Writing
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ and $T_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T^{cd}$ for the lowered tensor,
the equation reads $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$

**(ii) Matter content.** The equation constrains the metric and the matter of
the model jointly. A model specifies its matter sector as in
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]: a scalar-field model with its action
and stress-energy tensor ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), or a dust or perfect-fluid model with prescribed
stress-energy tensor and matter equations. The consistency condition that
every solution must satisfy, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, is not adopted separately; it
is a consequence of the equation and of the contracted second Bianchi identity
and is derived in [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]].

**(iii) Alternative presentation.** The action formulation of the same field
law is adopted separately in [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]. A
model adopts exactly one of the two presentations. They are alternative
presentations of one classical field law: the action-to-equation theorem of
this page identifies the equation obtained from stationarity of the total
action with the equation displayed in clause (i), and the direct presentation
is not an additional premise of an action-formulated model.

**(iv) Status and scope.** The equation is an adopted law of the model. It is
not derived from mathematical symmetry, from the equivalence principle, or
from observation; covariance and correspondence arguments motivate but do not
prove it. No numerical value of $c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted, and no
claim is made that any particular metric or matter configuration solves the
equation or describes nature. The smooth-branch exclusions of
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] apply: distributional or
lower-dimensional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, and non-smooth
fields are outside this formulation. Comparisons of a model's predictions with
data test the combined model — geometry, matter content and this law — and
agreement is evidence about that combination, not a proof of the postulate.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]], the following statements
about the matter content of a model.

**(i) Matter content is model input.** A model of the framework specifies its
nongravitational fields or matter and their explicit equations of motion and
couplings. The geometric data $(M,g,N)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and covariance of the model's equations
under relabelling of events do not select those fields, equations or couplings:
different matter specifications over the same geometry are different models of
the framework, and no dynamical selection principle is asserted.

**(ii) Smooth matter and its stress-energy tensor.** The matter of a model on
its matter domain is represented by smooth fields on an open domain
$U\subseteq M$, and the model's stress-energy tensor is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on $U$ of
[[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], with the unit reading recorded there.
The relation of $T$ to the matter fields is part of the model: a model derived
from an action defines $T$ as the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of that action,
while a model that prescribes $T$ directly is a separate source model.

**(iii) Consistency with the field law.** Where a model prescribes $T$
independently of matter fields, the prescription is admissible only if it meets
the consistency conditions imposed by the gravitational field law adopted for
the model, stated where that law is stated; in the action formulation the
matter equations, their coupling to the metric, and the on-shell conservation
of $T$ are derived within the model rather than assumed. Conservation is an
on-shell statement about a specified model and is not automatic for an
arbitrary smooth symmetric $T$.

**(iv) Energy conditions are optional additional assumptions.** A model may
adopt any of the pointwise inequalities of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]] as
further assumptions on its stress-energy tensor. None of them is a consequence
of the preceding clauses, of the field law, or of the symmetry of $T$; each
model records which conditions, if any, it adopts, and a model that adopts none
is not thereby excluded.

**(v) Scope and exclusions.** Idealizations such as unmodeled self-force,
finite-size and tidal corrections, dispersion, dissipation, and quantum effects
are outside the framework unless the model's explicit equations include them;
matter concentrated in a distributional or lower-dimensional source, and
matter configurations whose fields fail to be smooth on the model domain, are
outside the stated smooth branch and require additional mathematics. The
adoption of a matter model is not a claim that it describes nature.

three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and symmetric $2$-tensor $K$,

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of
